**Section 1.03 --- Accounting Terms**

All accounting terms not specifically or completely defined herein shall be construed in conformity with, and all financial data (including financial ratios and other financial calculations) required to be submitted pursuant to this Agreement shall be prepared in conformity with, GAAP applied on a consistent basis, as in effect from time to time, applied in a manner consistent with that used in preparing the audited financial statements delivered to the Administrative Agent on or prior to the Closing Date. If at any time any change in GAAP would affect the computation of any financial ratio or requirement set forth in any Loan Document, and either the Borrower or the Required Lenders shall so request, the Administrative Agent, the Lenders, and the Borrower shall negotiate in good faith to amend such ratio or requirement to preserve the original intent thereof in light of such change in GAAP; provided that, until so amended, such ratio or requirement shall continue to be computed in accordance with GAAP prior to such change therein.

**Section 1.04 --- SOFR Provisions**

**(a) Benchmark Replacement.** Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein or in any other Loan Document, if a Benchmark Transition Event occurs with respect to SOFR, the Administrative Agent and the Borrower may amend this Agreement to replace SOFR with a Benchmark Replacement. Any such amendment shall become effective at 5:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) on the fifth Business Day after the Administrative Agent has posted such proposed amendment to all Lenders and the Borrower, unless, prior to such time, Lenders comprising the Required Lenders have delivered to the Administrative Agent written notice that such Lenders do not accept such amendment. No replacement of SOFR with a Benchmark Replacement pursuant to this Section 1.04 will require the consent of any other party to this Agreement.

**(b) Conforming Changes.** In connection with the implementation of a Benchmark Replacement, the Administrative Agent will have the right to make Benchmark Replacement Conforming Changes from time to time and, notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein or in any other Loan Document, any amendments implementing such Benchmark Replacement Conforming Changes will become effective without any further action or consent of any other party to this Agreement.

**(c) Benchmark Transition Event.** "Benchmark Transition Event" means the occurrence of one or more of the following events with respect to SOFR: (i) a public statement or publication of information by or on behalf of the administrator of SOFR announcing that such administrator has ceased or will cease to provide SOFR permanently or indefinitely, (ii) a public statement by a Governmental Authority having jurisdiction over the administrator of SOFR or the Financial Stability Oversight Council announcing that SOFR is no longer representative, or (iii) a determination by the Administrative Agent that the circumstances described in clause (i) or (ii) have occurred with respect to SOFR.

**(d) Benchmark Replacement.** "Benchmark Replacement" means, for any Benchmark Transition Event, the first alternative set forth in the order below that can be determined by the Administrative Agent: (i) the sum of (A) the alternate benchmark rate that has been selected by the Administrative Agent and the Borrower giving due consideration to any evolving or then-prevailing market convention and (B) the related adjustment, if any; or (ii) the sum of (A) the alternate benchmark rate that has been selected by the Administrative Agent giving due consideration to any evolving or then-prevailing market convention and (B) the related adjustment, if any.

**[ARTICLE II --- THE CREDITS]{.underline}**

**Section 2.01 --- Revolving Commitments**

Subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein, each Lender severally agrees to make revolving loans (each such loan, a "**Revolving Loan**" and, collectively, the "**Revolving Loans**") to the Borrower from time to time during the Availability Period in an aggregate principal amount outstanding at any time that will not result in (a) such Lender\'s Revolving Exposure exceeding such Lender\'s Commitment, or (b) the aggregate Revolving Exposure of all Lenders exceeding the lesser of (i) the Aggregate Commitments and (ii) the Borrowing Base then in effect. Within the limits of each Lender\'s Commitment and subject to the foregoing limitations, the Borrower may borrow, prepay, and reborrow Revolving Loans during the Availability Period. The "**Availability Period**" means the period from and including the Closing Date to but excluding the Maturity Date (or such earlier date on which the Commitments are terminated in accordance with the terms hereof). The Commitment of each Lender as of the Closing Date and the aggregate percentage share of each Lender are set forth on Schedule 2.01. The Aggregate Commitments as of the Closing Date equal One Hundred Seventy-Five Million Dollars ($175,000,000).

**Section 2.02 --- Borrowings**

**(a) Borrowing Request.** Each Borrowing shall be made upon the Borrower\'s delivery to the Administrative Agent of a duly completed and executed Borrowing Request not later than 1:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) (i) three (3) Business Days prior to the requested date of any SOFR Borrowing, or (ii) one (1) Business Day prior to the requested date of any Base Rate Borrowing. Each such Borrowing Request shall specify (A) whether the requested Borrowing is to be a SOFR Borrowing or a Base Rate Borrowing, (B) the requested date of the Borrowing (which shall be a Business Day), (C) the aggregate principal amount of the Borrowing, and (D) in the case of a SOFR Borrowing, the initial Interest Period applicable thereto.

**(b) Minimum Amounts.** Each Borrowing shall be in a minimum aggregate principal amount of Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000) or a whole multiple of One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) in excess thereof (or, if less, the entire remaining amount of the Aggregate Commitments or the Borrowing Base then available).

**(c) Irrevocability.** Each Borrowing Request shall be irrevocable and binding on the Borrower.

**(d) Pro Rata Funding.** Upon receipt of a Borrowing Request, the Administrative Agent shall promptly notify each Lender of the details thereof and of the amount of such Lender\'s pro rata share of the requested Borrowing. Each Lender shall make the amount of its pro rata share of each Borrowing available to the Administrative Agent in immediately available funds at the Administrative Agent\'s office not later than 1:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) on the requested date of the Borrowing. Upon satisfaction (or waiver) of the applicable conditions set forth in Article IV, the Administrative Agent shall make all amounts received from the Lenders available to the Borrower in immediately available funds by crediting the Borrower\'s account designated for such purpose.

**Section 2.03 --- Borrowing Base**

**(a) Borrowing Base Limitation.** The aggregate outstanding principal amount of all Revolving Loans shall not at any time exceed the lesser of (i) the Aggregate Commitments and (ii) the Borrowing Base then in effect.

**(b) Borrowing Base Calculation.** The Borrowing Base at any time shall equal the sum of (i) eighty-five percent (85%) of Eligible Accounts Receivable at such time, plus (ii) sixty-five percent (65%) of Eligible Inventory at such time, minus (iii) Reserves at such time, all as reflected in the most recently delivered Borrowing Base Certificate.

**(c) Borrowing Base Certificates.** The Borrower shall deliver to the Administrative Agent a Borrowing Base Certificate on a monthly basis (and more frequently if requested by the Administrative Agent during a Dominion Period), setting forth the Borrowing Base as of the last day of the immediately preceding calendar month, within twenty (20) days after the end of each calendar month.

**(d) Borrowing Base Deficiency.** If at any time the aggregate outstanding principal amount of all Revolving Loans exceeds the Borrowing Base then in effect (a "**Borrowing Base Deficiency**"), the Borrower shall within two (2) Business Days after receipt of written notice from the Administrative Agent (or, if earlier, the date on which the Borrower becomes aware of such deficiency) prepay the Revolving Loans in an amount sufficient to eliminate such Borrowing Base Deficiency.

**Section 2.04 --- Interest**

**(a) Interest Rate.** Subject to the provisions of this Section, each Revolving Loan shall bear interest at a rate per annum equal to SOFR for the applicable Interest Period plus the Applicable Margin. The Applicable Margin shall range from 1.75% per annum to 2.50% per annum, determined by reference to the Total Leverage Ratio as set forth in the pricing grid in Section 1.01.

**(b) Default Interest.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of any Event of Default, the outstanding principal amount of all Revolving Loans and, to the extent permitted by applicable law, all other Obligations, shall bear interest at an additional rate of two percent (2.00%) per annum above the rate otherwise applicable (the "**Default Rate**"). Interest at the Default Rate shall accrue from the date of such Event of Default until such Event of Default is cured or waived. Payment or acceptance of the increased rate of interest provided for in this Section is not a permitted alternative to timely payment and shall not constitute a waiver of any Event of Default or otherwise prejudice or limit any rights or remedies of the Administrative Agent or any Lender.

**(c) Interest Periods.** Each SOFR Borrowing shall have an "**Interest Period**" of one (1), three (3), or six (6) months, as selected by the Borrower in the applicable Borrowing Request; provided that (i) any Interest Period that would otherwise end on a day that is not a Business Day shall be extended to the next succeeding Business Day unless such Business Day falls in the next calendar month, in which case such Interest Period shall end on the next preceding Business Day, and (ii) no Interest Period shall extend beyond the Maturity Date.

**(d) Payment of Interest.** Accrued interest on each Revolving Loan shall be payable in arrears on (i) the last day of each Interest Period applicable to such Loan, (ii) in the case of any Interest Period of more than three months\' duration, on the date that falls every three months after the beginning of such Interest Period, and (iii) on the Maturity Date.

**(e) Computation.** All computations of interest hereunder shall be made on the basis of a 360-day year and the actual number of days elapsed.

**Section 2.05 --- Commitment Fees**

The Borrower shall pay to the Administrative Agent, for the account of each Lender in accordance with its pro rata share, a commitment fee (the "**Commitment Fee**") equal to the Commitment Fee Rate (0.30% per annum) multiplied by the daily average amount by which the Aggregate Commitments exceed the aggregate outstanding principal amount of Revolving Loans during the applicable quarter. The Commitment Fee shall accrue from and including the Closing Date and shall be payable quarterly in arrears on the last Business Day of each March, June, September, and December, beginning with the first such date to occur after the Closing Date, and on the Maturity Date.

**Section 2.06 --- Repayment and Prepayment**

**(a) Maturity.** All outstanding principal of, and all accrued and unpaid interest on, the Revolving Loans, together with all other Obligations then due and payable, shall be due and payable in full on the Maturity Date (June 15, 2030).

**(b) Voluntary Prepayments.** The Borrower may, at any time and from time to time, prepay Revolving Loans in whole or in part without premium or penalty, upon delivery of a notice to the Administrative Agent not later than (i) 1:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) three (3) Business Days prior to any prepayment of SOFR Loans and (ii) 1:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) one (1) Business Day prior to any prepayment of Base Rate Loans. Each voluntary partial prepayment shall be in a minimum aggregate principal amount of One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) or a whole multiple of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($500,000) in excess thereof.

**(c) Mandatory Prepayments.** The Borrower shall prepay the Revolving Loans to the extent necessary to eliminate any Borrowing Base Deficiency as provided in Section 2.03(d). The Borrower shall also prepay the Revolving Loans to the extent that the aggregate outstanding principal amount of all Revolving Loans exceeds the Aggregate Commitments after giving effect to any reduction thereof.

**(d) Application of Prepayments.** Each prepayment of Revolving Loans shall be applied ratably among the Lenders in accordance with their respective pro rata shares. Any prepayment of a SOFR Loan on a day other than the last day of the applicable Interest Period shall be accompanied by any applicable breakage costs.

**Section 2.07 --- Payments Generally**

**(a) Currency and Funds.** All payments to be made by the Borrower hereunder shall be made in Dollars, in immediately available funds, without set-off, counterclaim, or other deduction of any nature, to the Administrative Agent at its office at 600 Commerce Tower, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202 (or such other address as the Administrative Agent may specify from time to time), for distribution to the Lenders in accordance with their respective pro rata shares.

**(b) Timing.** Each payment hereunder shall be made not later than 2:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) on the date when due. Any payment received by the Administrative Agent after 2:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) on any day shall be deemed to have been received on the next succeeding Business Day.

**(c) Insufficient Funds.** If at any time insufficient funds are received by and available to the Administrative Agent to pay fully all amounts then due and payable hereunder, such funds shall be applied first to the payment of fees and expenses due and payable hereunder, second to the payment of interest then due and payable, and third to the payment of principal then due and payable, ratably among the Lenders.

**(d) Taxes.** All payments hereunder shall be made free and clear of and without deduction for any present or future taxes, levies, imposts, duties, deductions, withholdings, assessments, fees, or other charges imposed by any Governmental Authority, except as required by applicable law.

**[ARTICLE III --- BORROWING BASE DETAILS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.01 --- Eligible Accounts Receivable**

An account receivable of any Loan Party shall be an "**Eligible Account Receivable**" at any time of determination if it satisfies each of the following criteria at such time: (a) such account arises from the sale of goods or the rendering of services by a Loan Party in the ordinary course of business; (b) such account represents a bona fide obligation of the account debtor for goods sold and delivered or services performed; (c) such account is not more than ninety (90) days past the original invoice date and not more than sixty (60) days past the original due date; (d) the account debtor is not the subject of any insolvency proceeding; (e) the account debtor is organized under the laws of the United States or Canada (or, if organized under the laws of any other jurisdiction, is supported by a letter of credit or credit insurance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent); (f) the aggregate amount of accounts receivable due from such account debtor does not exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of all Eligible Accounts Receivable (provided that the amount in excess of such twenty-five percent (25%) concentration limit shall be excluded); (g) such account is not subject to any dispute, offset, counterclaim, or defense asserted by the account debtor; (h) such account is not evidenced by a promissory note or chattel paper; (i) the Loan Party has not received notice of the death or dissolution of the account debtor; and (j) the Administrative Agent has not exercised its Permitted Discretion to exclude such account as ineligible. The Administrative Agent shall have the right, at any time and from time to time, in its Permitted Discretion, to establish, modify, or eliminate criteria for eligibility of accounts receivable.

**Section 3.02 --- Eligible Inventory**

Inventory of any Loan Party shall be "**Eligible Inventory**" at any time of determination if it satisfies each of the following criteria at such time: (a) such inventory is owned by a Loan Party, free and clear of all Liens (other than Permitted Liens and Liens in favor of the Administrative Agent); (b) such inventory is located at a location within the United States identified on a schedule delivered to the Administrative Agent; (c) such inventory consists of finished goods or raw materials (and not work-in-process, supplies, packaging materials, or obsolete, slow-moving, or defective goods); (d) such inventory is not subject to any consignment arrangement; (e) such inventory is covered by insurance as required under this Agreement; and (f) the Administrative Agent has not exercised its Permitted Discretion to exclude such inventory as ineligible. The Administrative Agent shall have the right, at any time and from time to time, in its Permitted Discretion, to establish, modify, or eliminate criteria for eligibility of inventory.

**Section 3.03 --- Reserves**

The Administrative Agent may, in its Permitted Discretion, from time to time establish, modify, or eliminate Reserves against the Borrowing Base. Such Reserves may include, without limitation, reserves for (a) rent and charges due to landlords at locations where Collateral is stored, (b) dilution of accounts receivable, (c) customs duties, (d) seasonal adjustments, and (e) any other factors that the Administrative Agent reasonably determines may impair the value or collectability of the Collateral.

**Section 3.04 --- Borrowing Base Reporting**

The Borrower shall deliver to the Administrative Agent a Borrowing Base Certificate, in form and detail satisfactory to the Administrative Agent, on a monthly basis as specified in Section 2.03(c). During the continuance of any Default or Event of Default, or at any time that the aggregate Revolving Exposure exceeds eighty percent (80%) of the lesser of (x) the Aggregate Commitments and (y) the Borrowing Base (a "**Dominion Period**"), the Borrower shall deliver Borrowing Base Certificates on a weekly basis. Each Borrowing Base Certificate shall be accompanied by such supporting documentation as the Administrative Agent may reasonably request, including aging reports, inventory reports, and accounts receivable schedules.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- EVENTS OF DEFAULT]{.underline}**

**Section 8.01 --- Events of Default**

Each of the following shall constitute an "**Event of Default**":

**(a) Non-Payment of Principal.** The Borrower shall fail to pay when due and payable (whether at the Maturity Date, by acceleration, or otherwise) any principal of any Revolving Loan.

**(b) Non-Payment of Interest or Fees.** The Borrower shall fail to pay within three (3) Business Days after the date when due any interest on any Revolving Loan or any fee or other amount payable hereunder or under any other Loan Document.

**(c) Incorrect Representations.** Any representation or warranty made or deemed made by or on behalf of any Loan Party in or in connection with this Agreement or any other Loan Document, or in any certificate, report, financial statement, or other document furnished pursuant to or in connection with this Agreement or any other Loan Document, shall prove to have been incorrect or misleading in any material respect when made or deemed made.

**(d) Breach of Negative or Financial Covenants.** Any Loan Party shall fail to perform or observe any term, covenant, or agreement contained in Article VII (including any financial covenant set forth in Section 7.09), and such failure shall not be subject to any grace or cure period.

**(e) Breach of Other Covenants.** Any Loan Party shall fail to perform or observe any other term, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement or any other Loan Document (other than those referred to in clauses (a), (b), and (d) of this Section 8.01), and such failure shall not be cured within thirty (30) days after the earlier of (i) notice thereof from the Administrative Agent to the Borrower and (ii) the date on which such failure first becomes known to any Responsible Officer of any Loan Party.

**(f) Cross-Default.** Any Loan Party or any Subsidiary shall (i) default in any payment of any Indebtedness (including, without limitation, the Subordinated Notes) beyond the applicable grace period with respect thereto, if any, or (ii) default in the observance or performance of any agreement or condition relating to any such Indebtedness or contained in any instrument or agreement evidencing, securing, or relating thereto, or any other event shall occur or condition exist, the effect of which default or other event or condition is to cause, or permit the holder or holders of such Indebtedness (or a trustee or agent on behalf of such holders) to cause, with the giving of notice if required, such Indebtedness to become due prior to its stated maturity; provided that it shall be an Event of Default under this clause (f) only if the aggregate principal amount of all such Indebtedness referred to in clauses (i) and (ii) exceeds Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000).

**(g) Bankruptcy and Insolvency.** Any Loan Party or any Subsidiary shall (i) commence any case, proceeding, or other action under any existing or future law relating to bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, or relief of debtors, seeking to have an order for relief entered with respect to it or seeking to adjudicate it as bankrupt or insolvent, or seeking reorganization, arrangement, adjustment, winding-up, liquidation, dissolution, composition, or other relief with respect to it or its debts, (ii) commence any case, proceeding, or other action seeking appointment of a receiver, trustee, custodian, conservator, or other similar official for it or for all or any substantial part of its assets, or (iii) make a general assignment for the benefit of its creditors; or any case, proceeding, or other action shall be commenced against any Loan Party or any Subsidiary under any existing or future law relating to bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, or relief of debtors, which remains undismissed for a period of sixty (60) days; or any Loan Party or any Subsidiary shall take any action in furtherance of, or indicating its consent to, approval of, or acquiescence in, any of the acts referred to above.

**(h) Judgments.** One or more judgments or orders for the payment of money in an aggregate amount in excess of Ten Million Dollars ($10,000,000) (to the extent not covered by insurance as to which the insurer has acknowledged coverage or by an indemnity from a creditworthy third party) shall be rendered against any Loan Party or any Subsidiary and the same shall remain unsatisfied, undischarged, unvacated, unbonded, or unstayed for a period of sixty (60) consecutive days after the entry thereof.

**(i) ERISA Events.** An ERISA Event shall have occurred that, individually or in the aggregate, would reasonably be expected to result in liability of the Loan Parties in an aggregate amount exceeding Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000).

**(j) Change of Control.** A Change of Control shall have occurred.

**(k) Invalidity of Loan Documents or Liens.** Any Loan Document at any time after its execution and delivery and for any reason other than as expressly permitted hereunder ceases to be in full force and effect, or any Lien purported to be created by any Security Document ceases to be a valid and perfected Lien (having the priority required by this Agreement or the applicable Security Document) on any material portion of the Collateral, except to the extent that such loss of perfection or priority results from the failure of the Administrative Agent to maintain possession of certificates evidencing equity interests or to file UCC continuation statements.

**(l) Guaranty Invalid.** Any provision of the Guaranty set forth in Article X shall at any time for any reason cease to be valid and binding on any Guarantor, or any Guarantor shall so state in writing, or any Guarantor shall deny or disaffirm its obligations under the Guaranty.

**(m) Material Adverse Effect.** Any event, circumstance, or condition shall have occurred that has had a Material Adverse Effect.

**(a)** If any Event of Default shall have occurred and be continuing, the Administrative Agent may, and at the request of the Required Lenders shall, by notice to the Borrower, take any or all of the following actions:

> \(i\) declare the Commitments terminated, whereupon the obligation of each Lender to make any further Revolving Loans shall immediately terminate;

**[3. Presentation of the Proposed Credit Facility]{.underline}**

Ms. Engstrom and Thomas P. Nguyen, Chief Financial Officer and a director of the Corporation, presented the details of the proposed senior secured revolving credit facility (the "Credit Facility") to the Board. The presentation covered, among other things, the following principal terms and conditions:

**Facility Type and Amount.** The Credit Facility would consist of a senior secured revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of up to $150,000,000 (One Hundred Fifty Million Dollars). The Credit Facility would be available on a revolving basis, subject to customary borrowing base limitations and conditions to borrowing set forth in the Credit Agreement.

**Lender Syndicate and Administrative Agent.** The Credit Facility would be provided by a syndicate of lenders (collectively, the "Lenders") led by Ridgeline National Bank, a national banking association, which would serve as the administrative agent (the "Administrative Agent"). The syndicate would additionally include Harborview Capital Finance, LLC, Greystone Commercial Lending Corp., and Meridian Trust Company, each in its capacity as a Lender, with initial commitments allocated among the Lenders as set forth in the term sheet previously distributed to the Board.

**Maturity.** The Credit Facility would have a maturity date of five (5) years from the closing date.

**Interest Rate.** Borrowings under the Credit Facility would bear interest at a rate per annum equal to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") plus an applicable margin, with the applicable margin determined by reference to a pricing grid based on the Corporation\'s consolidated leverage ratio.

**Security.** The obligations of the Corporation under the Credit Facility would be secured by a first-priority security interest in and lien upon substantially all assets of the Corporation, including, without limitation, all accounts receivable, inventory, equipment, general intangibles, intellectual property, equity interests in subsidiaries, deposit accounts, securities accounts, and all proceeds of the foregoing.

**Guaranties.** The Corporation\'s parent company, Pinnacle Holdings Corp., a Delaware corporation, and each of the Corporation\'s direct and indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries --- Pinnacle Fastener Technologies, Inc., a Delaware corporation, Pinnacle Coatings & Surface Solutions, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, and Pinnacle Aerospace Components, Inc., an Ohio corporation --- would provide guaranties of the Corporation\'s obligations under the Credit Facility and the related Loan Documents.

**Use of Proceeds.** Proceeds of the Credit Facility would be used for working capital, general corporate purposes, and the refinancing of existing indebtedness, including the full repayment and termination of the Corporation\'s existing credit facility with Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp.

Mr. Nguyen further presented financial projections and analyses demonstrating the Corporation\'s ability to service the proposed indebtedness and comply with the financial covenants contemplated by the Credit Agreement. Mr. Nguyen noted that the Credit Facility would provide the Corporation with enhanced liquidity and financial flexibility to support its ongoing operations, capital expenditure programs, and strategic growth initiatives.

The Chairperson referenced the materials previously distributed to each member of the Board, including a term sheet dated May 12, 2025, a substantially final draft of the Credit Agreement, and the financial projections prepared by management. These materials had been provided to the directors no later than May 22, 2025, affording the Board adequate time for review and consideration.

A thorough discussion ensued among the directors regarding the business rationale for the proposed Credit Facility, the competitiveness of the proposed terms and pricing relative to market conditions, the impact of the proposed security arrangements on the Corporation\'s operational flexibility, the financial covenants and reporting obligations to be undertaken by the Corporation, and the strategic importance of refinancing the existing facility with Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp. in light of that facility\'s approaching maturity. Each director had the opportunity to ask questions and receive responses from Mr. Nguyen and Ms. Engstrom. After full discussion and deliberation, the Board determined that entry into the Credit Facility on the terms presented was in the best interests of the Corporation and its stockholders.

**[4. Resolutions Adopted]{.underline}**

After further discussion, upon motion duly made by James E. Carruthers, seconded by Sandra L. Whitmore, and unanimously approved by all directors present, the following resolutions were adopted:

**RESOLVED,** that the Corporation be, and hereby is, authorized to enter into a senior secured revolving credit facility (the "Credit Facility") in an aggregate principal amount of up to $150,000,000 (One Hundred Fifty Million Dollars) (the "Commitment Amount"), with a syndicate of lenders led by Ridgeline National Bank, as Administrative Agent (the "Administrative Agent"), pursuant to the terms and conditions of a Credit Agreement substantially in the form presented to this Board of Directors (the "Credit Agreement"), with such changes thereto as any Authorized Officer (as defined below) may approve, such approval to be conclusively evidenced by such officer\'s execution and delivery thereof.

**[Section 2: Amended and Restated Bylaws]{.underline}**

Effective March 15, 2020 Adopted by resolution of the Board of Directors on March 15, 2020

**2.1 Article I --- Offices**

**Section 1.1 --- Principal Office.** The principal office of the Corporation shall be located at 4200 Industrial Parkway, Suite 300, Akron, Ohio 44306, or at such other place as the Board of Directors may from time to time designate.

**Section 1.2 --- Other Offices.** The Corporation may also have offices at such other places, both within and without the State of Delaware, as the Board of Directors may from time to time determine or as the business of the Corporation may require.

**2.2 Article II --- Meetings of Stockholders**

**Section 2.1 --- Annual Meeting.** The annual meeting of the stockholders of the Corporation for the election of directors and for the transaction of such other business as may properly come before the meeting shall be held on such date and at such time as shall be designated from time to time by the Board of Directors.

**Section 2.2 --- Special Meetings.** Special meetings of the stockholders may be called at any time by the Board of Directors, the Chairperson of the Board, or the Chief Executive Officer. Business transacted at any special meeting of stockholders shall be limited to the purposes stated in the notice of such meeting.

**Section 2.3 --- Notice.** Written notice of each meeting of stockholders, whether annual or special, stating the place, date, and hour of the meeting and, in the case of a special meeting, the purpose or purposes for which the meeting is called, shall be given not less than ten (10) nor more than sixty (60) days before the date of the meeting to each stockholder of record entitled to vote at such meeting.

**Section 2.4 --- Quorum.** The holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of capital stock entitled to vote thereat, present in person or represented by proxy, shall constitute a quorum at any meeting of stockholders. If a quorum is present, the affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the shares of stock represented at the meeting and entitled to vote on the subject matter shall be the act of the stockholders, unless a greater number of votes is required by the Certificate of Incorporation, these Bylaws, or applicable law.

**Section 2.5 --- Voting.** Each share of Common Stock shall entitle the holder thereof to one (1) vote on each matter submitted to a vote of stockholders.

**2.3 Article III --- Board of Directors**

**Section 3.1 --- Number and Term.** The number of directors constituting the entire Board of Directors shall be not fewer than three (3) nor more than nine (9), as fixed from time to time by resolution of the Board of Directors. The current number of directors is five (5). Each director shall hold office until the next annual meeting of stockholders and until such director\'s successor shall have been duly elected and qualified, or until such director\'s earlier death, resignation, or removal. Directors may be elected to serve consecutive terms without limitation.

**Section 3.2 --- Quorum.** A majority of the total number of directors then in office shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the Board of Directors. In no event shall a quorum be less than one-third (1/3) of the total number of directors. For purposes of this Section, the total number of directors then in office shall be the number of directors last fixed by the Board of Directors, unless one or more vacancies exist, in which case the total number of directors then in office shall be the number of directors last fixed by the Board of Directors minus the number of vacancies.

**Section 3.3 --- Voting / Action by the Board.** The vote of a majority of the directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present shall be the act of the Board of Directors, unless a greater number is required by the Certificate of Incorporation, these Bylaws, or applicable law. Each director present at a meeting at which a quorum is present shall have one (1) vote. A director who is present at a meeting and abstains from voting shall be counted for purposes of determining whether a quorum is present but shall not be counted as voting in favor of or against any proposal.

**Section 3.4 --- Action by Written Consent.** Any action required or permitted to be taken at any meeting of the Board of Directors or of any committee thereof may be taken without a meeting if all members of the Board of Directors or committee, as the case may be, consent thereto in writing or by electronic transmission, and the writing or writings or electronic transmission or transmissions are filed with the minutes of proceedings of the Board of Directors or committee. Such consent shall have the same force and effect as a unanimous vote of the Board of Directors or committee at a duly convened meeting. For the avoidance of doubt, action by written consent under this Section 3.4 requires the consent of all directors then in office, and not merely a majority thereof.

**Section 3.5 --- Special Meetings of the Board.** Special meetings of the Board of Directors may be called by the Chairperson of the Board, the Chief Executive Officer, or any two (2) directors. Notice of the time and place of each special meeting shall be given to each director by at least twenty-four (24) hours\' prior notice, which notice may be given personally, by telephone, by electronic mail, or by other electronic transmission. Neither the business to be transacted at, nor the purpose of, any special meeting of the Board of Directors need be specified in the notice of such meeting unless required by law, the Certificate of Incorporation, or these Bylaws.

**Section 3.6 --- Committees.** The Board of Directors may designate one or more committees, each consisting of one or more directors. Each committee shall have and may exercise such powers as shall be conferred or authorized by resolution of the Board of Directors. No committee shall have the power or authority to approve any action that requires approval of the full Board of Directors under the Certificate of Incorporation, these Bylaws, or applicable law.

**Section 3.7 --- Vacancies.** Any vacancy on the Board of Directors, whether resulting from death, resignation, removal, or an increase in the number of directors, shall be filled by the affirmative vote of a majority of the remaining directors, even if less than a quorum, or by a sole remaining director. A director elected to fill a vacancy shall hold office until the next annual meeting of stockholders and until such director\'s successor shall have been duly elected and qualified.

**2.4 Article IV --- Officers**

**Section 4.1 --- Officers Generally.** The officers of the Corporation shall be a Chief Executive Officer, a Chief Financial Officer, a Secretary, and such other officers as the Board of Directors may from time to time designate, elect, or appoint. Any two or more offices may be held by the same person, except that the Chief Executive Officer and the Secretary shall not be the same person unless the Board of Directors expressly resolves otherwise. Officers shall be elected by the Board of Directors and shall hold office at the pleasure of the Board.

**Section 4.2 --- Chief Executive Officer.** The Chief Executive Officer shall be the chief executive officer of the Corporation and shall have general supervision over the business and affairs of the Corporation, subject to the direction and control of the Board of Directors. The Chief Executive Officer shall preside at all meetings of the stockholders and of the Board of Directors at which he or she is present, unless a separate Chairperson of the Board has been designated. The Chief Executive Officer shall have the power to sign and execute all authorized deeds, mortgages, bonds, contracts, agreements, and other instruments in the name of and on behalf of the Corporation, except where the signing and execution thereof shall be expressly delegated by the Board of Directors or these Bylaws to some other officer or agent of the Corporation or shall be required by law to be otherwise signed or executed.

**Section 4.3 --- Chief Financial Officer.** The Chief Financial Officer shall have charge of the financial affairs of the Corporation and shall keep or cause to be kept accurate books of account. The Chief Financial Officer shall have the power to sign and execute all authorized financial instruments, agreements, and documents on behalf of the Corporation, including but not limited to checks, drafts, notes, and other evidences of indebtedness, credit agreements, security agreements, and related financing documents.

**Section 4.4 --- General Counsel.** The General Counsel shall be the chief legal officer of the Corporation and shall oversee all legal matters affecting the Corporation and its subsidiaries. The General Counsel shall advise the Board of Directors and the officers of the Corporation on legal matters and shall supervise outside counsel retained by the Corporation. The General Counsel shall not be deemed an officer for purposes of executing instruments binding the Corporation to third parties unless specifically authorized by the Board of Directors by resolution adopted at a duly convened meeting or by unanimous written consent. Nothing in this Section 4.4 shall be construed to grant the General Counsel signatory authority over credit agreements, guaranty agreements, security agreements, or other financing documents unless such authority is expressly conferred by the Board of Directors.

**Section 4.5 --- Secretary.** The Secretary shall keep or cause to be kept the minutes of all meetings of the stockholders, the Board of Directors, and any committees thereof. The Secretary shall give or cause to be given all notices required by law, the Certificate of Incorporation, or these Bylaws.

**[Section 4: Code of Regulations]{.underline}**

Adopted April 22, 2012, as amended through the date hereof

**4.1 Article I --- Meetings of Shareholders**

**Section 1.1 --- Annual Meeting.** The annual meeting of shareholders for the election of directors and the transaction of such other business as may properly come before the meeting shall be held on such date and at such time as may be designated by the Board of Directors.

**Section 1.2 --- Special Meetings.** Special meetings of shareholders may be called by the president, by the Board of Directors, or by the holders of not less than twenty-five percent (25%) of the outstanding shares of the Corporation entitled to vote at such meeting. Only business related to the purposes set forth in the notice of the special meeting shall be conducted at any special meeting.

**Section 1.3 --- Notice.** Written notice of each meeting of shareholders shall be given to each shareholder of record entitled to vote at such meeting not less than ten (10) nor more than sixty (60) days prior to the date of the meeting, stating the place, date, and time of the meeting and, in the case of a special meeting, the purpose or purposes for which the meeting is called.

**Section 1.4 --- Quorum.** The holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of the Corporation entitled to vote thereat, present in person or represented by proxy, shall constitute a quorum at any meeting of shareholders. In the absence of a quorum, a majority of the shares so represented may adjourn the meeting from time to time without further notice.

**4.2 Article II --- Board of Directors**

**Section 2.1 --- Number.** The Board of Directors shall consist of three (3) directors. The number of directors may be changed only by amendment to the Articles of Incorporation or this Code of Regulations, as applicable, adopted by the shareholders of the Corporation. Each director shall be a natural person who is at least eighteen years of age.

**Section 2.2 --- Quorum and Voting.** A majority of the whole authorized number of directors shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the Board of Directors. For the avoidance of doubt, with a Board fixed at three (3) directors, a quorum shall require the presence of at least two (2) directors. When a quorum is present, the act of a majority of the directors present at a meeting shall be the act of the Board of Directors. For the further avoidance of doubt, with a quorum of two (2) directors, the affirmative vote of at least two (2) directors shall be required for any action of the Board. No action may be taken by the Board of Directors at any meeting at which a quorum is not present, except to adjourn the meeting to a later date. A director who is present at a meeting and abstains from voting shall be counted for purposes of determining whether a quorum is present but shall not be counted as voting in favor of or against any resolution or motion.

**Section 2.3 --- Action Without a Meeting.** Any action which may be authorized or taken at a meeting of the directors may be authorized or taken without a meeting with the affirmative vote or approval of, and in a writing or writings signed by, all of the directors, which writing or writings shall be filed with or entered upon the records of the Corporation. Such written consent shall have the same force and effect as a unanimous vote of the directors at a duly convened meeting. No action may be taken by written consent unless all three (3) directors consent thereto in writing. A written consent that is signed by fewer than all of the directors shall be of no force or effect.

**Section 2.4 --- Special Meetings.** Special meetings of the Board of Directors may be held at any time upon call of the president or any two (2) directors. Notice of the time and place of each special meeting shall be given to each director by at least forty-eight (48) hours\' prior notice, delivered personally, by telephone, by electronic mail, or by other means reasonably calculated to provide actual notice to the director. The notice need not specify the business to be transacted at the meeting unless required by law, the Articles of Incorporation, or this Code of Regulations. \(a\) *General Limitation.* The Company shall not, and shall not permit any Subsidiary to, create, incur, assume, guarantee, or otherwise become directly or indirectly liable with respect to any Indebtedness, except for Permitted Indebtedness.

\(c\) *Capital Lease Obligations.* The Company shall not, and shall not permit any Subsidiary to, enter into or assume any Capital Lease Obligations if, after giving effect thereto, the aggregate outstanding amount of all Capital Lease Obligations of the Company and its Subsidiaries would exceed Ten Million Dollars ($10,000,000).

**Section 7.02. Limitation on Liens.** The Company shall not, and shall not permit any Subsidiary to, create, incur, assume, or suffer to exist any Lien on any of its property or assets, whether now owned or hereafter acquired, except for Permitted Liens.

**Section 7.03. Limitation on Fundamental Changes.** The Company shall not, and shall not permit any Subsidiary to, merge into or consolidate with any other Person, or permit any other Person to merge into or consolidate with it, or sell, transfer, lease, or otherwise dispose of (in one transaction or in a series of transactions) all or substantially all of its assets, or all or substantially all of the stock of any Subsidiary, except with the prior written consent of the Purchaser, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

Limitation on Restricted Payments.** The Company shall not, and shall not permit any Subsidiary to, declare or make, or agree to declare or make, directly or indirectly, any Restricted Payment, except (a) dividends payable solely in common stock of the Company, (b) Restricted Payments to the Parent Guarantor in an aggregate amount not exceeding Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) in any fiscal year for the purpose of paying general and administrative expenses of the Parent Guarantor, and (c) Restricted Payments to the Parent Guarantor in amounts necessary to pay taxes attributable to the consolidated group of which the Company is a member, in each case so long as no Default or Event of Default has occurred and is continuing or would result therefrom.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- EVENTS OF DEFAULT (Selected Provisions)]{.underline}**

**Section 8.01. Events of Default.** Each of the following shall constitute an "Event of Default" under this Agreement:

\(a\) *Failure to Pay.* The Company fails to pay (i) any principal of any Note when the same becomes due and payable, whether at stated maturity, by acceleration, or otherwise, or (ii) any interest on any Note or any fee or other amount payable under this Agreement within five (5) Business Days after the same becomes due and payable.

\(b\) *Breach of Covenants.* The Company fails to observe or perform any covenant, condition, or agreement contained in Article VII (Negative Covenants), and such failure continues for a period of fifteen (15) days after the earlier of (i) written notice thereof by the Purchaser to the Company and (ii) the date on which a Responsible Officer of the Company first becomes aware of such failure.

\(c\) *Cross-Default.* (i) The Company or any Subsidiary fails to make any payment when due (whether by scheduled maturity, required prepayment, acceleration, demand, or otherwise) in respect of any Indebtedness (other than the Notes) having an aggregate outstanding principal amount of more than Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000); or (ii) any event or condition occurs that results in any such Indebtedness becoming due prior to its scheduled maturity or that enables or permits (with or without the giving of notice, the lapse of time, or both) the holder or holders of any such Indebtedness or any trustee or agent on its or their behalf to cause any such Indebtedness to become due, or to require the prepayment, repurchase, redemption, or defeasance thereof, prior to its scheduled maturity; *provided* that this clause (c) shall not apply to secured Indebtedness that becomes due as a result of the voluntary sale or transfer of the property or assets securing such Indebtedness if such sale or transfer is permitted hereunder and the repayment of such Indebtedness is made concurrently with such sale or transfer.

\(d\) *Breach of Representations.* Any representation or warranty made or deemed made by the Company or the Parent Guarantor in this Agreement or in any certificate, report, financial statement, or other document delivered pursuant hereto proves to have been incorrect in any material respect when made or deemed made.

\(e\) *Bankruptcy.* The Company or any Subsidiary commences any proceeding under any bankruptcy, reorganization, insolvency, dissolution, or liquidation law of any jurisdiction, whether now or hereafter in effect, or has any such proceeding commenced against it which remains undismissed for a period of sixty (60) days, or consents to the appointment of, or taking possession by, a receiver, liquidator, assignee, custodian, trustee, sequestrator, or similar official of the Company or any Subsidiary or of any substantial part of its property.

\(f\) *Judgments.* One or more judgments for the payment of money in an aggregate amount in excess of Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000) (to the extent not covered by independent third-party insurance as to which the insurer does not dispute coverage) shall be rendered against the Company, any Subsidiary, or any combination thereof, and shall remain undischarged for a period of thirty (30) consecutive days during which execution shall not be effectively stayed, or any action shall be legally taken by a judgment creditor to attach or levy upon any assets of the Company or any Subsidiary to enforce any such judgment.

**[5.1 Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp. --- Unterminated All-Assets Filing (Filing #2)]{.underline}**

**Issue:** UCC-1 Financing Statement File No. 2019-4572810, filed August 9, 2019, by Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp. against Pinnacle Manufacturing Group, Inc. at the Delaware Secretary of State, covering "all assets" of the Borrower, whether now owned or hereafter acquired, remains active as of the Search Date (June 8, 2025). A UCC-3 Continuation Statement (File No. 2024-3681045) was filed on July 22, 2024, extending the lapse date from August 9, 2024, to August 9, 2029. No UCC-3 Termination Statement appears in the Delaware Secretary of State records as of the Search Date.

**Background:** Counsel for the Borrower has represented that the prior credit facility between the Borrower and Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp. (the "Prior Facility") is being refinanced and repaid in full in connection with the closing of the Credit Facility on June 15, 2025. Counsel to Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp. has indicated that a UCC-3 Termination Statement with respect to File No. 2019-4572810 has been prepared and is expected to be filed in connection with the payoff and termination of the Prior Facility. However, as of the Search Date, the official records of the Delaware Secretary of State do not reflect the filing or indexing of any UCC-3 Termination Statement with respect to this financing statement.

**Impact on Opinion:** The filing of an effective UCC-3 Termination Statement by Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp. (or, alternatively, the authorized filing of a termination statement by the Borrower as debtor under UCC § 9-509(d)(2) following receipt of a termination demand under UCC § 9-513) is a prerequisite to rendering an unqualified opinion that the security interests granted in favor of Ridgeline National Bank, as Administrative Agent, constitute first-priority perfected security interests in the personal property collateral of the Borrower. So long as the Ironbridge filing remains active on the records of the Delaware Secretary of State, the Ironbridge security interest (if it continues to secure outstanding obligations) would have priority over the Ridgeline filing by virtue of first-to-file priority under UCC § 9-322(a)(1). Even if the underlying indebtedness to Ironbridge has been fully repaid and the security interest has been released as a matter of contract, an active UCC financing statement on the public record may give rise to priority disputes with future creditors or purchasers who rely on the public filing record, and may prevent counsel from rendering a clean first-priority opinion.

**Recommended Action:**

> \(a\) *Confirm Filing of Termination Statement.* Confirm that the UCC-3 Termination Statement has been or will be filed with the Delaware Secretary of State simultaneously with or prior to the closing of the Credit Facility on June 15, 2025, and obtain a post-filing search or a filing acknowledgment/receipt from the Delaware Secretary of State confirming the effectiveness of the termination;
>
> \(b\) *Obtain Executed Termination Statement.* If the termination statement has not yet been filed, obtain from Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp. an executed UCC-3 Termination Statement referencing File No. 2019-4572810 for immediate filing by counsel;
>
> \(c\) *Opinion Qualification.* If the termination of the Ironbridge filing cannot be confirmed prior to the opinion delivery date, include an express assumption in the closing opinion letter that the Ironbridge filing will have been terminated at or prior to the time of closing, or alternatively, qualify the first-priority lien opinion to except the Ironbridge filing and note that the opinion is subject to confirmation of termination. The Administrative Agent should be notified of this qualification in advance of closing.

**[5.2 Great Lakes Tax Authority --- State Tax Lien (Filing #9)]{.underline}**

**Issue:** A state tax lien filing by the Great Lakes Tax Authority, Ohio Department of Revenue, File No. OH-2024-TL-0048271, filed March 3, 2024, against Pinnacle Manufacturing Group, Inc. at the Ohio Secretary of State, covering "all property and rights to property, whether real or personal, tangible or intangible," in the amount of $347,218.64, remains active with no release, satisfaction, or subordination agreement on file as of the Search Date.

**Background:** This filing indicates that the Great Lakes Tax Authority has assessed unpaid state taxes, together with associated penalties and interest, against the Borrower pursuant to Ohio Revised Code Chapter 5739 (relating to the Ohio commercial activity tax) and/or Chapter 5747 (relating to Ohio income tax and employer withholding tax). State tax liens arising under Ohio law are created by operation of statute and attach to all property and rights to property of the taxpayer. The amount of the assessed lien is $347,218.64, which, while not material relative to the $175,000,000 Credit Facility, represents a lien with potential statutory super-priority that could impair the Administrative Agent\'s first-priority security interest in the Borrower\'s assets.

**Impact on Opinion:** State tax liens arising under Ohio statutory authority typically enjoy statutory priority and may prime consensual security interests, including security interests previously perfected by UCC filing. See Ohio Revised Code §§ 5739.13 and 5747.13 (providing that tax liens constitute a first lien upon all property of the taxpayer, subject to certain limited exceptions). The existence of this active, unreleased state tax lien means that counsel cannot render an unqualified opinion that the security interests in favor of Ridgeline National Bank, as Administrative Agent, constitute first-priority liens on the assets of the Borrower. Although the UCC-1 financing statement filed in Delaware by the Administrative Agent is the proper filing for perfection of a security interest in the Borrower\'s personal property under UCC Article 9, the Ohio state tax lien constitutes a separate, non-UCC lien with potential statutory priority that may attach to the Borrower\'s property wherever located, including property located in or connected to Ohio, where the Borrower maintains its principal place of business and substantially all of its tangible assets.

In addition, the existence of this tax lien raises questions regarding the accuracy of the Borrower\'s representations and warranties in the Credit Agreement with respect to (i) the payment of taxes (Section 5.09 of the Credit Agreement), (ii) the absence of liens other than Permitted Liens (Section 5.08 of the Credit Agreement), and (iii) the accuracy of the officer\'s certificate to be delivered at closing with respect to tax matters. These representations should be reviewed in light of this finding.

**Recommended Action:**

> \(a\) *Payment and Release.* The Borrower should pay the outstanding tax obligation in the amount of $347,218.64 (or such other amount as may be confirmed by the Great Lakes Tax Authority as the current balance due, including any additional accrued penalties and interest) and obtain a written release or certificate of satisfaction of the state tax lien from the Great Lakes Tax Authority, and cause such release to be filed with the Ohio Secretary of State, prior to the closing of the Credit Facility;
>
> \(b\) *Subordination Agreement.* Alternatively, the Borrower should obtain a subordination agreement from the Great Lakes Tax Authority subordinating the state tax lien to the security interests of the Administrative Agent under the Security Agreement. Note, however, that state tax authorities may be unwilling to agree to subordination, and this approach may not be feasible;
>
> \(c\) *Opinion Qualification.* If the state tax lien cannot be released or subordinated prior to closing, the closing opinion must qualify the first-priority lien opinion to expressly except the state tax lien filed by the Great Lakes Tax Authority (File No. OH-2024-TL-0048271, in the amount of $347,218.64). The Administrative Agent and the Lenders should be informed of the existence of this lien and its potential impact on collateral priority. Additionally, the Borrower\'s compliance certificate and representations regarding the payment of taxes and the absence of material liens should be reviewed and, if necessary, updated or disclosed against.

para(d, '(b)\\t**Perfection by filing.** The Financing Statements are in appropriate form for filing in the office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware (as to the Borrower, the Parent Guarantor, PCSS and PAC) and the office of the Secretary of State of the State of Ohio (as to PFT). para(d, '(c)\\t**Deposit accounts.** (i) For each deposit account listed on Annex C that is maintained with Ridgeline National Bank, the Administrative Agent has \"control\" of that account within the meaning of Section 9-104(a)(1) of the UCC because the secured party is the bank at which the account is maintained. (ii) For each other deposit account listed on Annex C, upon execution and delivery of the applicable Deposit Account Control Agreement by the Grantor, the depositary bank and the Administrative Agent, the Administrative Agent has \"control\" within the meaning of Section 9-104(a)(2) of the UCC. We note that a security interest in a deposit account as original collateral cannot be perfected by filing.', indent=0.5, first=-0.5, align='justify')

 "(a)\t**Creation.** The Security Agreement [and the Pledge Agreement] create in favor of the Administrative Agent, for the benefit of the Secured Parties, a valid security interest under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the “**NY UCC**”) in each Grantor’s rights in the Collateral described therein, to the extent that Article 9 of the NY UCC applies to such Collateral (the “**UCC Collateral**”), as security for the Obligations.  "(b)\t**Perfection by filing.** The Financing Statements are in appropriate form for filing in the office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware (as to the Borrower, the Parent Guarantor, PCSS and PAC) and the office of the Secretary of State of the State of Ohio (as to PFT). Under Sections 9-301(1) and 9-307(e) of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of Delaware (the “**DE UCC**”) and Chapter 1309 of the Ohio Revised Code (the “**OH UCC**”), respectively, the local law of each such state governs perfection by filing of a security interest in the UCC Collateral of the Grantors organized in that state. Upon the filing of the Financing Statements in those offices (the search reports show these filings were made on June 10, 2025, under the file numbers on Annex B), the security interest in favor of the Administrative Agent in each Grantor’s UCC Collateral is perfected to the extent a security interest in such UCC Collateral can be perfected by filing a financing statement under the DE UCC or the OH UCC, as applicable.",
 "(c)\t**Deposit accounts.** (i) For each deposit account listed on Annex C that is maintained with Ridgeline National Bank, the Administrative Agent has “control” of that account within the meaning of Section 9-104(a)(1) of the UCC because the secured party is the bank at which the account is maintained. (ii) For each other deposit account listed on Annex C, upon execution and delivery of the applicable Deposit Account Control Agreement by the Grantor, the depositary bank and the Administrative Agent, the Administrative Agent has “control” within the meaning of Section 9-104(a)(2) of the UCC. In each case, the security interest in the deposit account is perfected by control under Sections 9-312(b)(1) and 9-314(a) of the UCC as in effect in the bank’s jurisdiction (determined under Section 9-304), assuming that jurisdiction is [the State of New York, Delaware or Ohio]. We note that a security interest in a deposit account as original collateral cannot be perfected by filing.",
 "(d)\t**Securities accounts.** For each securities account listed on Annex C, upon execution and delivery of the applicable Securities Account Control Agreement by the Grantor, the securities intermediary and the Administrative Agent (under which the securities intermediary agrees to comply with entitlement orders originated by the Administrative Agent without further consent of the Grantor), the Administrative Agent has “control” of the security entitlements carried in that account within the meaning of Sections 8-106(d)(2) and 9-106 of the UCC. The security interest in those security entitlements and the securities account is perfected by control under Section 9-314(a) of the UCC as in effect in the securities intermediary’s jurisdiction (determined under Section 8-110(e)), assuming that jurisdiction is [the State of New York, Delaware or Ohio] and that [Cromdale Consulting Wealth Advisors] is a “securities intermediary” within the meaning of Section 8-102(a)(14) of the UCC. The security interest in that investment property is also perfected by filing the Financing Statements against the Borrower and the Parent Guarantor in Delaware (Sections 9-305(c)(1) and 9-312(a) of the DE UCC). A security interest perfected by control, however, has priority over one perfected only by filing (Section 9-328(1)).",
 "(e)\t**Pledged equity.** (i) *Certificated securities.* The shares of the Borrower, PFT and PAC described on Annex E are certificated securities. Upon delivery to the Administrative Agent in the State of [New York] of the certificates representing those shares, indorsed to the Administrative Agent or in blank by an effective indorsement or accompanied by stock powers duly executed in blank, the Administrative Agent has “control” of those securities within the meaning of Section 8-106(b)(1) of the NY UCC.  "(f)\t**Intellectual property.** The security interest in the Grantors’ patents, trademarks and unregistered copyrights included in the UCC Collateral is perfected by the filing of the Financing Statements, to the extent perfection can be achieved by filing under the DE UCC or the OH UCC. TX 9-123-456 and TX 9-234-567), which may require recordation with the United States Copyright Office under the federal Copyright Act and the cases construing Section 9-311(a)(1) of the UCC, or (ii) the effect of recordation, or failure to record, with the United States Patent and Trademark Office as against subsequent purchasers or mortgagees.",
 "(g)\t**Priority — filed collateral.** The Search Report identifies no financing statement naming any Grantor as debtor and covering any UCC Collateral on file, as of June 8, 2025, in the office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware or the State of Ohio, other than (i) the Financing Statements and (ii) the filings described on Annex G. [Upon the filing of the UCC-3 termination statement relating to Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp. File No. 2019-4572810 on June [__], 2025,] the Administrative Agent’s security interest in UCC Collateral perfected by filing the Financing Statements will have priority under Section 9-322(a)(1) of the DE UCC or the OH UCC, as applicable, over any other security interest in that UCC Collateral created by the applicable Grantor and perfected only by filing a financing statement, except for the security interests of the secured parties named in the filings listed in Part 1 of Annex G in the collateral those filings describe.",
 "(h)\t**Priority — pledged certificated securities.** Assuming the Administrative Agent acquired its security interest in the certificated securities described on Annex E for value and without notice of any adverse claim (within the meaning of Section 8-105 of the NY UCC), the Administrative Agent (i) has acquired its interest free of any adverse claim as a “protected purchaser” under Section 8-303 of the NY UCC and (ii) has priority under Section 9-328(1) of the NY UCC over any security interest in those securities held by a secured party that does not have control."]:

para(d, "Except as expressly set forth in paragraphs 7(g) and 7(h), we express no opinion as to the priority of any security interest. In particular, we do not opine that the security interests constitute “first-priority” security interests subject only to Permitted Liens. We note the state tax lien notice described in Part 2 of Annex G.", align="justify")
para(d, N("(i) The June 9 letter asks for an unqualified first-priority opinion “subject only to Permitted Liens.” Under the TriBar reports that request is generally declined because priority depends on facts outside the record (non-filed liens, statutory liens, purchase-money interests, buyers in ordinary course, setoff and similar matters). We have instead given filing-based and control-based priority opinions and addressed each prior filing in the Search Report, as the letter requires. (ii) Paragraph 7(g) cannot be delivered until the Ironbridge all-assets financing statement (continued on July 22, 2024 through August 9, 2029) is terminated of record or a filed-stamped UCC-3 is in hand. (iii) The $347,218.64 Ohio state tax lien against the Borrower is not on Schedule 7.02, contradicts the tax representation in Section 5.08 of the Credit Agreement, and must be released (or, at minimum, disclosed and reserved against) before closing. (iv) The Search Report is dated through June 8, 2025 yet reports the June 10, 2025 filings; it needs a bring-down search and certified search results. (v) Schedule I to the Security Agreement describes 1,000,000 shares of PFT and 500,000 shares of PAC, but the articles and certificate of incorporation of PFT and PAC authorize and show outstanding only 1,000 shares each. Schedule I must be corrected and the certificates inspected before paragraph 7(e) is given. (vi) The Control Agreements, the identity and status of the securities intermediary, and the bank’s and intermediary’s jurisdictions must be confirmed before paragraphs 7(c) and 7(d) are given. (vii) The pledge of the PCSS membership interests requires the Sole Member’s written consent, executed by an Authorized Officer, under Section 4.1 of the PCSS LLC Agreement. Under 6 Del. C.  "(a)\t**Creation.** The Security Agreement [and the Pledge Agreement] create in favor of the Administrative Agent, for the benefit of the Secured Parties, a valid security interest under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the “**NY UCC**”) in each Grantor’s rights in the Collateral described therein, to the extent that Article 9 of the NY UCC applies to such Collateral (the “**UCC Collateral**”), as security for the Obligations.  "(b)\t**Perfection by filing.** The Financing Statements are in appropriate form for filing in the office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware (as to the Borrower, the Parent Guarantor, PCSS and PAC) and the office of the Secretary of State of the State of Ohio (as to PFT). Under Sections 9-301(1) and 9-307(e) of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of Delaware (the “**DE UCC**”) and Chapter 1309 of the Ohio Revised Code (the “**OH UCC**”), respectively, the local law of each such state governs perfection by filing of a security interest in the UCC Collateral of the Grantors organized in that state. Upon the filing of the Financing Statements in those offices (the search reports show these filings were made on June 10, 2025, under the file numbers on Annex B), the security interest in favor of the Administrative Agent in each Grantor’s UCC Collateral is perfected to the extent a security interest in such UCC Collateral can be perfected by filing a financing statement under the DE UCC or the OH UCC, as applicable.",
 "(c)\t**Deposit accounts.** (i) For each deposit account listed on Annex C that is maintained with Ridgeline National Bank, the Administrative Agent has “control” of that account within the meaning of Section 9-104(a)(1) of the UCC because the secured party is the bank at which the account is maintained. (ii) For each other deposit account listed on Annex C, upon execution and delivery of the applicable Deposit Account Control Agreement by the Grantor, the depositary bank and the Administrative Agent, the Administrative Agent has “control” within the meaning of Section 9-104(a)(2) of the UCC. In each case, the security interest in the deposit account is perfected by control under Sections 9-312(b)(1) and 9-314(a) of the UCC as in effect in the bank’s jurisdiction (determined under Section 9-304), assuming that jurisdiction is [the State of New York, Delaware or Ohio]. We note that a security interest in a deposit account as original collateral cannot be perfected by filing.",
 "(d)\t**Securities accounts.** For each securities account listed on Annex C, upon execution and delivery of the applicable Securities Account Control Agreement by the Grantor, the securities intermediary and the Administrative Agent (under which the securities intermediary agrees to comply with entitlement orders originated by the Administrative Agent without further consent of the Grantor), the Administrative Agent has “control” of the security entitlements carried in that account within the meaning of Sections 8-106(d)(2) and 9-106 of the UCC. The security interest in those security entitlements and the securities account is perfected by control under Section 9-314(a) of the UCC as in effect in the securities intermediary’s jurisdiction (determined under Section 8-110(e)), assuming that jurisdiction is [the State of New York, Delaware or Ohio] and that [Cromdale Consulting Wealth Advisors] is a “securities intermediary” within the meaning of Section 8-102(a)(14) of the UCC. The security interest in that investment property is also perfected by filing the Financing Statements against the Borrower and the Parent Guarantor in Delaware (Sections 9-305(c)(1) and 9-312(a) of the DE UCC). A security interest perfected by control, however, has priority over one perfected only by filing (Section 9-328(1)).",
 "(e)\t**Pledged equity.** (i) *Certificated securities.* The shares of the Borrower, PFT and PAC described on Annex E are certificated securities. Upon delivery to the Administrative Agent in the State of [New York] of the certificates representing those shares, indorsed to the Administrative Agent or in blank by an effective indorsement or accompanied by stock powers duly executed in blank, the Administrative Agent has “control” of those securities within the meaning of Section 8-106(b)(1) of the NY UCC.  "(f)\t**Intellectual property.** The security interest in the Grantors’ patents, trademarks and unregistered copyrights included in the UCC Collateral is perfected by the filing of the Financing Statements, to the extent perfection can be achieved by filing under the DE UCC or the OH UCC. TX 9-123-456 and TX 9-234-567), which may require recordation with the United States Copyright Office under the federal Copyright Act and the cases construing Section 9-311(a)(1) of the UCC, or (ii) the effect of recordation, or failure to record, with the United States Patent and Trademark Office as against subsequent purchasers or mortgagees.",
 "(g)\t**Priority — filed collateral.** The Search Report identifies no financing statement naming any Grantor as debtor and covering any UCC Collateral on file, as of June 8, 2025, in the office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware or the State of Ohio, other than (i) the Financing Statements and (ii) the filings described on Annex G. [Upon the filing of the UCC-3 termination statement relating to Ironbridge Industrial Finance Corp. File No. 2019-4572810 on June [__], 2025,] the Administrative Agent’s security interest in UCC Collateral perfected by filing the Financing Statements will have priority under Section 9-322(a)(1) of the DE UCC or the OH UCC, as applicable, over any other security interest in that UCC Collateral created by the applicable Grantor and perfected only by filing a financing statement, except for the security interests of the secured parties named in the filings listed in Part 1 of Annex G in the collateral those filings describe.",
 "(h)\t**Priority — pledged certificated securities.** Assuming the Administrative Agent acquired its security interest in the certificated securities described on Annex E for value and without notice of any adverse claim (within the meaning of Section 8-105 of the NY UCC), the Administrative Agent (i) has acquired its interest free of any adverse claim as a “protected purchaser” under Section 8-303 of the NY UCC and (ii) has priority under Section 9-328(1) of the NY UCC over any security interest in those securities held by a secured party that does not have control."]:

para(d, "Except as expressly set forth in paragraphs 7(g) and 7(h), we express no opinion as to the priority of any security interest. In particular, we do not opine that the security interests constitute “first-priority” security interests subject only to Permitted Liens. We note the state tax lien notice described in Part 2 of Annex G.", align="justify")
para(d, N("(i) The June 9 letter asks for an unqualified first-priority opinion “subject only to Permitted Liens.” Under the TriBar reports that request is generally declined because priority depends on facts outside the record (non-filed liens, statutory liens, purchase-money interests, buyers in ordinary course, setoff and similar matters). We have instead given filing-based and control-based priority opinions and addressed each prior filing in the Search Report, as the letter requires. (ii) Paragraph 7(g) cannot be delivered until the Ironbridge all-assets financing statement (continued on July 22, 2024 through August 9, 2029) is terminated of record or a filed-stamped UCC-3 is in hand. (iii) The $347,218.64 Ohio state tax lien against the Borrower is not on Schedule 7.02, contradicts the tax representation in Section 5.08 of the Credit Agreement, and must be released (or, at minimum, disclosed and reserved against) before closing. (iv) The Search Report is dated through June 8, 2025 yet reports the June 10, 2025 filings; it needs a bring-down search and certified search results. (v) Schedule I to the Security Agreement describes 1,000,000 shares of PFT and 500,000 shares of PAC, but the articles and certificate of incorporation of PFT and PAC authorize and show outstanding only 1,000 shares each. Schedule I must be corrected and the certificates inspected before paragraph 7(e) is given. (vi) The Control Agreements, the identity and status of the securities intermediary, and the bank’s and intermediary’s jurisdictions must be confirmed before paragraphs 7(c) and 7(d) are given. (vii) The pledge of the PCSS membership interests requires the Sole Member’s written consent, executed by an Authorized Officer, under Section 4.1 of the PCSS LLC Agreement. Under 6 Del. C.
