This opinion letter is delivered to you pursuant to Section 4.01(d) of the Credit Agreement. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings given to them in the Credit Agreement.

# I. Transaction Documents

This opinion letter relates to the following documents (collectively, the "**Transaction Documents**" and each a "**Transaction Document**"). Annex A sets forth the Opinion Parties that are party to each Transaction Document.

\(1\) the Credit Agreement dated as of June 15, 2025, among the Borrower, the Parent Guarantor, the Subsidiary Guarantors, the Lenders and the Administrative Agent, including the guaranty set forth in Article X thereof;

\(2\) the Security Agreement dated as of June 15, 2025, among the Borrower, the Parent Guarantor, PFT, PCSS and PAC, as grantors (the "**Grantors**"), in favor of the Administrative Agent (the "**Security Agreement**");

\(3\) the Pledge Agreement dated as of June 15, 2025, among \[the Borrower, the Parent Guarantor\] and the Administrative Agent (the "**Pledge Agreement**");

\(4\) the Guaranty Agreement dated as of June 15, 2025, by the Parent Guarantor and each Subsidiary Guarantor in favor of the Administrative Agent (the "**Guaranty Agreement**"); and

\(5\) each Deposit Account Control Agreement and Securities Account Control Agreement dated as of June 15, 2025 and listed on Annex C (collectively, the "**Control Agreements**").

**\[Note to Draft:** (a) The Pledge Agreement, the separate Guaranty Agreement and the Control Agreements have not yet been furnished to us; we cannot render any opinion on a document we have not reviewed. (b) The Credit Agreement defines "Guaranty" as Article X of the Credit Agreement, the Security Agreement recitals refer to a separately executed "Guaranty" and "Subsidiary Guaranties", the guarantor consents authorize a "Guaranty"/"Subsidiary Guaranty", and your June 9 letter refers to a separate Guaranty Agreement. Please confirm whether a stand-alone Guaranty Agreement will be executed; if not, item (4) will be deleted and the opinions will refer to Article X. (c) The Credit Agreement defines the Pledge Agreement as among "the Loan Parties", your letter describes it as among the Borrower, the Parent Guarantor and the Administrative Agent, and the Security Agreement (Section 2.02 and Schedule I) itself contains a pledge of the same equity. Parties to be conformed.**\]**

The UCC financing statements described on Annex B are referred to herein as the "**Financing Statements**."

# II. Documents Reviewed

In rendering the opinions expressed below, we have examined executed counterparts (or copies certified or otherwise identified to our satisfaction) of the Transaction Documents and the Financing Statements and the following documents (collectively with the Transaction Documents, the "**Reviewed Documents**"):

\(a\) the Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation of the Borrower filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on June 20, 2017 \[, as certified by the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on June \[\_\_\], 2025\], and the Amended and Restated Bylaws of the Borrower adopted March 15, 2020;

\(b\) the Certificate of Incorporation of the Parent Guarantor filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on January 8, 2007 \[, as certified by such Secretary of State on June \[\_\_\], 2025\], and the Bylaws of the Parent Guarantor \[complete copy to be furnished\];

\(c\) the Articles of Incorporation of PFT filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Ohio on April 22, 2012 \[, as certified by such Secretary of State on June \[\_\_\], 2025\], and the Code of Regulations of PFT adopted April 22, 2012, as amended;

\(d\) the Certificate of Formation of PCSS filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on September 15, 2016 \[, as certified by such Secretary of State on June \[\_\_\], 2025\], and the \[Amended and Restated\] Limited Liability Company Agreement of PCSS dated as of September 15, 2016, as amended (the "**PCSS LLC Agreement**");

\(e\) the Certificate of Incorporation of PAC filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on November 3, 2018 \[, as certified by such Secretary of State on June \[\_\_\], 2025\], and the Bylaws of PAC \[complete copy to be furnished\];

\(f\) the minutes of the special meeting of the Board of Directors of the Borrower held May 28, 2025 \[, as supplemented by the resolutions of the Board of Directors of the Borrower adopted June \[\_\_\], 2025 ratifying and authorizing Aggregate Commitments of \$175,000,000\], and the Secretary's Certificate of the Borrower dated June 15, 2025;

\(g\) \[the Unanimous Written Consent of the Board of Directors of the Parent Guarantor dated June \[\_\_\], 2025, executed by each director then in office (being, per its bylaws, Margaret R. Halstead, Thomas P. Nguyen and Patricia L. Cavanaugh)\];

head(d, "Part I — Bottom Line", 1)
para(d, "The accompanying advance draft of our closing opinion (closing-legal-opinion.docx) follows the June 9, 2025 requirements letter from Raymond K. Drummond (Drummond & Associates LLP). That breach ripens into a Terracotta Event of Default and then a cross-default under Credit Agreement Section 8.01(f). def issue(code, title, sev, facts, impact, action):

head(d, "A. Substantive Conflicts and Covenant Issues", 2)
issue("A-1","Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement — $125 million Senior Secured Indebtedness cap breached","G",
 "Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement (Terracotta) Section 7.01(b) bars the Borrower or any Subsidiary from incurring or guaranteeing Senior Secured Indebtedness if aggregate Senior Secured Indebtedness, “including … the aggregate amount of all undrawn commitments under any revolving credit facility,” would exceed $125,000,000. The Section 1.01 definition repeats the undrawn-commitment rule. Aggregate Commitments are $175,000,000 (Credit Agreement Schedule 2.01). Other secured debt on Schedule 7.01 includes the Aldersgate capital lease obligations (approximately $4.8 million) and the Stanton lease (approximately $85,000). Total: about $179.9 million, roughly $54.9 million over the cap. Schedule 5.04 discloses the covenant but not the breach. The Terracotta “Permitted Liens” clause (i) covers Senior Credit Facility liens only “subject to the limitations set forth in Section 7.01(b)”, so Section 7.02 is breached as well.",
 "No-conflicts opinion 5(iii) cannot be given without a specific exception, which the draft carries as Annex F, item 1. Under Terracotta Section 8.01(b), the breach becomes an Event of Default 15 days after notice or a Responsible Officer’s awareness. Once it does, the approximately $18.75 million of Subordinated Notes may be accelerated, which is a cross-default under Credit Agreement Section 8.01(f) ($5 million threshold). Representations in Credit Agreement Section 5.03(a)(iii) and Security Agreement Section 3.04(c) are untrue at signing, so the Officer’s Certificate Sections 3, 4 and 8 cannot be signed as drafted. The Section 4.01(m) condition (subordination confirmation satisfactory to the Agent) is unmet. Terracotta Article IX subordinates the Notes to all “Senior Indebtedness” without a dollar cap, but Terracotta would likely argue that debt incurred in breach of its covenant falls outside its consent. Lenders will want that foreclosed.",
 "(1) Obtain an amendment to or consent under the Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement, executed by Terracotta before closing, that raises the cap to at least about $180 million (or excludes undrawn revolving commitments) and confirms the Credit Facility is “Senior Indebtedness”/a “Senior Credit Facility”. Any later amendment requires Required Lender consent under Credit Agreement Section 7.08. (2) Obtain the subordination acknowledgment or intercreditor agreement required by Section 4.01(m). (3) Alternative: reduce Aggregate Commitments to no more than about $120.1 million ($125.0 million less about $4.885 million of other secured debt), which is a business-deal change for the Lenders. (4) Tell Drummond now; the letter asks for identified conflicts.")
issue("A-2","Terracotta facts inconsistent; possible missed amortization payment; Parent Guarantor is a Terracotta obligor","H",
 "The Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement excerpt shows 9.50% notes with **annual** principal payments of $3,125,000 beginning April 1, 2023. Credit Agreement Schedule 7.01 shows 10.50% interest and **semi-annual** payments of about $1,562,500 beginning October 1, 2023. On the Terracotta schedule, three payments (April 2023, 2024 and 2025) leave $15,625,000 outstanding, not the $18,750,000 the Credit Agreement and Officer’s Certificate report. The Parent Guarantor is a party to and guarantor under Terracotta Article VI, but Schedule 5.04 lists only the Borrower. The excerpt misidentifies Ironbridge as administrative agent of the new facility and gives a Seattle address for W&C. Officer’s Certificate Schedule B shows $3.5 million of Restricted Payments over the last twelve months. Terracotta Section 7.05 permits only up to $2 million a year for Parent G&A, plus tax distributions.",
 "If the April 1, 2025 principal installment was not paid, there is a payment Event of Default under Terracotta Section 8.01(a) (no grace period for principal), which is an immediate cross-default under Credit Agreement Section 8.01(f) and makes the no-Default certification false. Any unrecorded amendment (rate or amortization) is a Material Agreement change we have not reviewed. The no-conflicts opinion for the Parent Guarantor must also cover Terracotta.",
 "Obtain the complete executed Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement with all amendments, the payment history, and a Terracotta payoff/status letter confirming principal outstanding and no default. Conform Schedules 5.04 and 7.01. Confirm the character of the $3.5 million in Restricted Payments. Re-certify the excerpts; the current certification contains obvious errors.")
issue("A-3","Korvin License Agreement — anti-pledge clause; consent not obtained","G",
 "Korvin Section 14.2(a) bars any pledge, security interest or encumbrance of the agreement or the License Rights, Licensed Patents or Licensed Technology without Korvin’s consent, which Korvin may withhold in its sole discretion. Section 14.2(b) makes a violating Transfer void *ab initio*. Section 14.3 provides injunctive relief and termination on 30 days’ notice if uncured. Security Agreement Section 2.01(g) expressly grants a lien on “all rights of the Borrower under” the Korvin license. The General Intangibles definition, by contrast, covers Korvin rights only “to the extent assignable or encumberable”, an internal inconsistency. Schedule 5.04 says no consent has been obtained. Credit Agreement Section 5.12 calls the license “material to the conduct of the Borrower’s business”. Security Agreement Section 3.07(d) represents that the IP grant breaches no license and needs no third-party consent; that is false. The Officer’s Certificate cites an Amendment No. 1 (March 15, 2022) that we have not seen. Korvin is mislabeled a “Copyright License” in the Security Agreement. The license term is inconsistent across documents: Korvin “Term” runs to expiry of the last Licensed Patent; Schedule 5.15 says 15 years plus two five-year renewals; Security Agreement Schedule IV says an initial term expiring August 31, 2030. The licensed patents are also described inconsistently (Schedule 5.15 lists U.S. Patent Nos. 9,876,543, 10,234,567 and 10,345,678; Schedule IV refers to a “Korvin European Patent-family”).",
 "This is an actual conflict, carried as Annex F, item 2. Under NY UCC Section 9-408(a) and (c), the anti-assignment clause is ineffective to prevent attachment and perfection of a security interest in the licensee’s general intangible, and to trigger default or termination on account of the grant. Under Section 9-408(d), however, the Agent cannot enforce, use or assign the license against Korvin, so the collateral value is minimal. Whether federal patent law displaces Section 9-408 for an exclusive patent license is unsettled; the draft takes it as qualification (k). The litigation and termination risk is an MAE consideration.",
 "Obtain Korvin’s written consent to the grant, ideally with an estoppel and licensor acknowledgment. If that is not obtainable before closing, amend the Security Agreement to make the Korvin license an Excluded Asset except to the extent Section 9-408 renders the restriction ineffective, and correct Security Agreement Sections 2.01(g) and 3.07(d), Credit Agreement Section 5.03, and the “Copyright License” definition. Obtain the full agreement and Amendment No. 1. Conform the term and patent descriptions.")
issue("A-4","Officer’s Certificate: pro forma covenant failure on a $175 million initial borrowing; wrong sections; historical test","G",
 "Officer’s Certificate Section 4 refers to “the initial borrowing under the Credit Facility in the aggregate principal amount of $175,000,000”. Section 5 and Schedule B test “Section 7.11”, which does not exist; the financial covenants are in Section 7.09. They test only historically as of March 31, 2025, using the Ironbridge balance of $118,750,000, whereas Sections 4.01(e)(iii) and 4.01(l) require pro forma compliance after the initial Borrowing. The FCCR deducts total capex ($8.5 million) rather than Unfinanced Capital Expenditures. No Borrowing Base Certificate has been furnished, and a full $175 million draw requires the Borrowing Base to be at least $175 million.",
 "Using the certificate’s own figures (EBITDA $50.0 million; Subordinated Notes $18.75 million; capital leases and other $5.0 million): a $175 million draw gives Consolidated Funded Indebtedness of $198.75 million and a Total Leverage Ratio of **3.98x**, above the 3.50x maximum. That is an immediate Event of Default under Section 8.01(d) (no cure period), and Section 4.02(c) blocks funding. The largest initial revolving draw consistent with 3.50x is about $151.25 million. A draw equal to the Ironbridge payoff ($118.75 million) produces 2.85x. We do not opine on financial calculations (qualification (n)), but we cannot rely on assumption (7) for a certificate we know to be inaccurate.",
 "Confirm the actual initial Borrowing amount and the Borrowing Base. Re-issue the Officer’s Certificate and deliver the Compliance Certificate (Exhibit B) with a correct Section 7.09 pro forma calculation (including pro forma interest on the new facility and Unfinanced Capex). Delete or correct the $175,000,000 initial-borrowing recital.")

 ["As certified (Ironbridge balance, 3/31/25)","$118.75M","$18.75M","$5.00M","$142.50M","$50.0M","2.85x","Compliant"],
 ["Initial borrowing = Ironbridge payoff","$118.75M","$18.75M","$5.00M","$142.50M","$50.0M","2.85x","Compliant"],

 widths=[1.7,0.7,0.7,0.8,0.8,0.7,0.5,0.7], size=8.5)

head(d, "B. Authorization, Execution and Incumbency", 2)
issue("B-1","Borrower board authorization — $150 million authorized; board roster conflict; notice; misdescribed subsidiaries","G",
 "The May 28, 2025 minutes, Resolution 1 and Secretary’s Certificate paragraph 6 authorize a facility “up to $150,000,000”, while the Credit Agreement provides $175,000,000. The resolution approves the Credit Agreement “substantially in the form presented” with officer-approved changes; a 16.7% increase in principal is not a conforming change. The minutes record five directors present (Halstead, Nguyen, Sandra L. Whitmore, James E. Carruthers, Robert A. Feinberg) as “the entire membership of the Board”. The Organizational Documents Package, certified by the Secretary on June 12, 2025, lists the directors as Halstead, Nguyen, David T. Okonkwo, Patricia L. Cavanaugh and Robert M. Jennings. Okonkwo appears in the minutes only as a non-director. Bylaws Section 3.2 sets the quorum at a majority of five (three). If the certified roster is correct, only two directors attended and no quorum existed. The minutes cite notice under “Section 3.06” of the Bylaws (48 hours); the Bylaws’ special-meeting notice provision is Section 3.5 (24 hours). The minutes recite both proper notice and waivers from directors “who had not received timely formal notice”. The resolutions describe PFT as a Delaware corporation and PAC as an Ohio corporation (it is the reverse).",
 "Opinion 3(a) (due authorization) cannot be given, and opinion 4 depends on it. Credit Agreement Section 4.01(b)(iii) requires resolutions authorizing the Loan Documents. The Secretary’s Certificate is internally inconsistent with the closing.",
 "Determine the true board composition from stockholder election records or the Parent Guarantor’s stockholder consents. Before signing, have the Borrower’s directors of record adopt a unanimous written consent under DGCL Section 141(f) and Bylaws Section 3.4. The consent should authorize the $175,000,000 facility and each Loan Document by name (Credit Agreement, Security Agreement, Pledge Agreement, Guaranty, Control Agreements), correct the subsidiaries’ jurisdictions, and ratify prior acts. If any act has already occurred, consider DGCL Section 204 ratification. Obtain the notice waivers. Re-issue the Secretary’s Certificate.")
issue("B-2","Parent Guarantor written consent not signed by the directors of record","G",
 "The Tab A consent (May 30, 2025) recites a two-member board (Halstead and Robert J. Castellano) and is signed by those two. The Organizational Documents Package (Part V) says the Parent Guarantor’s bylaws fix a three-member board of Halstead, Nguyen and Patricia L. Cavanaugh, and incorrectly states that the consent was adopted by “all three directors”. DGCL Section 141(f) requires the written consent of all directors in office.",
 "The consent is ineffective unless Castellano is a duly elected director and the board in fact has two members, which contradicts the certified bylaws summary. Opinions 3(b) and 4 cannot be given for the Parent Guarantor (its guaranty, its grant under the Security Agreement, and the pledge of 4,500,000 Borrower shares).",
 "Obtain the complete Parent Guarantor bylaws and director election records. Adopt a new unanimous written consent signed by every director of record that authorizes the Credit Agreement (Article X), Security Agreement, Pledge Agreement and any Guaranty Agreement. Correct the Organizational Documents Package certification.")
issue("B-3","PFT written consent — signed by one purported director; directors do not match the Articles","G",
 "The Tab B consent lists directors Sandra M. Kowalski, James D. Hartwell and Patricia L. Moreno, and only Kowalski signed. PFT’s Articles (Article Fifth) and Code of Regulations (Section 2.1) fix a board of three: Halstead, Nguyen and Okonkwo, “the current directors”. ORC Section 1701.54 and Code Section 2.3 require a writing signed by **all** directors; Section 2.3 says a consent signed by fewer than all directors “shall be of no force or effect”. The consent also states PFT’s principal office as Suite 340, whereas the Articles state Suite 300 and Security Agreement Schedule III states Youngstown, Ohio.",
 "There is no valid PFT authorization, so opinions 3(c) and 4 fail for PFT.",
 "Adopt a new written consent signed by all three directors of record, or evidence a valid change of directors by shareholder action. The consent should approve the Credit Agreement (Article X), the Security Agreement and any Guaranty Agreement by name.")
issue("B-4","PCSS Sole Member consent signed by a person without authority; LLC agreement versions conflict; pledge consent missing","G",
 "The Tab C consent is executed for the Sole Member (the Borrower) by David T. Okonkwo, General Counsel. Under both versions of the PCSS LLC Agreement furnished to us, only the CEO or CFO of the Sole Member is an “Authorized Officer”: Section 2.4 in the Organizational Documents Package version, and Sections 3.2 and 12.4 in the Exhibit 1 “Amended and Restated” version. Section 2.4 expressly excludes the General Counsel. Section 2.3(c)–(d) requires Sole Member consent for any guaranty over $500,000 and **any** grant of a security interest, and makes action without such consent “void and of no force or effect”. Borrower Bylaws Section 4.4 also denies the General Counsel signatory authority over financing documents absent express board authorization. The two LLC agreement versions differ in title, section numbering and consent thresholds: Section 2.3 versus Section 8.3(c), which uses $500,000 individually and $1,000,000 in the aggregate. Section 4.1 bars any pledge of the membership interests without a Member consent executed by an Authorized Officer. No such consent has been delivered for the pledge in Security Agreement Section 2.02(a)(ii).",
 "PCSS’s guaranty and grant are void under its own LLC agreement until a proper consent is delivered, so opinions 3(d), 4 and 7 fail as to PCSS. The pledge of the PCSS interests is also restricted: DLLCA Section 18-1101(g) makes UCC Sections 9-406 and 9-408 inapplicable to LLC interests, so the restriction is enforceable.",
 "Have Halstead or Nguyen re-execute the Sole Member consent, covering the guaranty, Security Agreement grant and Credit Agreement joinder, plus a separate Section 4.1 consent to the pledge of 100% of the PCSS interests. Obtain a certified complete copy of the operative LLC agreement and all amendments. Consider an Article 8 opt-in amendment and certificated interest if the Lenders want control-based priority (Security Agreement Section 4.02(e) contemplates an amendment).")
issue("B-5","PAC written consent — signed by a non-director; a director of record did not sign","G",
 "The Tab D consent recites directors Nguyen and Karen A. Westbrook and is signed by them. PAC’s Certificate of Incorporation (Article V) lists the directors as Halstead and Nguyen and states that a unanimous written consent “requires the consent of both directors.” Halstead did not sign.",
 "The consent fails DGCL Section 141(f), so opinions 3(e) and 4 fail for PAC.",
 "Adopt a new unanimous written consent signed by Halstead and Nguyen, or evidence a valid election of Westbrook, approving the Credit Agreement (Article X), the Security Agreement and any Guaranty Agreement.")
issue("B-6","Signatories and incumbency — guarantor signers are not officers of record; inconsistent across documents; no incumbency certificates","G",
 "PFT signed the Credit Agreement through James A. Whitmore (Vice President) and the Security Agreement through Richard S. Calloway (President). PAC signed through Sandra L. Fujikawa (Vice President) and Jennifer A. Marcos (President), respectively. The governing documents of both PFT and PAC list only Halstead (President) and Nguyen (Secretary/Treasurer) as officers. Each guarantor consent authorizes “any officer”, but no evidence of these individuals’ appointment and no incumbency certificate has been furnished for the Parent Guarantor, PFT, PCSS or PAC (Credit Agreement Section 4.01(b)(iv)). The Agent’s signatory appears as “Christopher D. Cromdale Consulting” in the Credit Agreement and “Christopher D. Engelman” in the Security Agreement. “Cromdale Consulting” is also the name of the securities intermediary in Schedule V, which suggests a document-assembly error.",
 "The execution and delivery limb of opinion 3 cannot be given. The genuineness assumption (assumption 1) excludes Opinion Party officers, so we must verify the signers’ incumbency.",
 "Either have Halstead or Nguyen execute for PFT and PAC, or deliver board resolutions appointing the named officers together with incumbency and specimen-signature certificates for every Opinion Party. Flag the Agent signature-block errors to Drummond.")

Drummond’s letter asks us to advise “as soon as possible” if we foresee any inability to deliver a requested opinion; we recommend sending the draft today with the cover note in Part VI.", align="justify")

head(d, "A. Substantive Conflicts and Covenant Issues", 2)
issue("A-1","Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement — $125 million Senior Secured Indebtedness cap breached","G",
 "Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement (Terracotta) Section 7.01(b) bars the Borrower or any Subsidiary from incurring or guaranteeing Senior Secured Indebtedness if aggregate Senior Secured Indebtedness, “including … the aggregate amount of all undrawn commitments under any revolving credit facility,” would exceed $125,000,000. The Section 1.01 definition repeats the undrawn-commitment rule. Aggregate Commitments are $175,000,000 (Credit Agreement Schedule 2.01). Other secured debt on Schedule 7.01 includes the Aldersgate capital lease obligations (approximately $4.8 million) and the Stanton lease (approximately $85,000). Total: about $179.9 million, roughly $54.9 million over the cap. Schedule 5.04 discloses the covenant but not the breach. The Terracotta “Permitted Liens” clause (i) covers Senior Credit Facility liens only “subject to the limitations set forth in Section 7.01(b)”, so Section 7.02 is breached as well.",
 "No-conflicts opinion 5(iii) cannot be given without a specific exception, which the draft carries as Annex F, item 1. Under Terracotta Section 8.01(b), the breach becomes an Event of Default 15 days after notice or a Responsible Officer’s awareness. Once it does, the approximately $18.75 million of Subordinated Notes may be accelerated, which is a cross-default under Credit Agreement Section 8.01(f) ($5 million threshold). Representations in Credit Agreement Section 5.03(a)(iii) and Security Agreement Section 3.04(c) are untrue at signing, so the Officer’s Certificate Sections 3, 4 and 8 cannot be signed as drafted. The Section 4.01(m) condition (subordination confirmation satisfactory to the Agent) is unmet. Terracotta Article IX subordinates the Notes to all “Senior Indebtedness” without a dollar cap, but Terracotta would likely argue that debt incurred in breach of its covenant falls outside its consent. Lenders will want that foreclosed.",
 "(1) Obtain an amendment to or consent under the Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement, executed by Terracotta before closing, that raises the cap to at least about $180 million (or excludes undrawn revolving commitments) and confirms the Credit Facility is “Senior Indebtedness”/a “Senior Credit Facility”. Any later amendment requires Required Lender consent under Credit Agreement Section 7.08. (2) Obtain the subordination acknowledgment or intercreditor agreement required by Section 4.01(m). (3) Alternative: reduce Aggregate Commitments to no more than about $120.1 million ($125.0 million less about $4.885 million of other secured debt), which is a business-deal change for the Lenders. (4) Tell Drummond now; the letter asks for identified conflicts.")
issue("A-2","Terracotta facts inconsistent; possible missed amortization payment; Parent Guarantor is a Terracotta obligor","H",
 "The Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement excerpt shows 9.50% notes with **annual** principal payments of $3,125,000 beginning April 1, 2023. Credit Agreement Schedule 7.01 shows 10.50% interest and **semi-annual** payments of about $1,562,500 beginning October 1, 2023. On the Terracotta schedule, three payments (April 2023, 2024 and 2025) leave $15,625,000 outstanding, not the $18,750,000 the Credit Agreement and Officer’s Certificate report. The Parent Guarantor is a party to and guarantor under Terracotta Article VI, but Schedule 5.04 lists only the Borrower. The excerpt misidentifies Ironbridge as administrative agent of the new facility and gives a Seattle address for W&C. Officer’s Certificate Schedule B shows $3.5 million of Restricted Payments over the last twelve months. Terracotta Section 7.05 permits only up to $2 million a year for Parent G&A, plus tax distributions.",
 "If the April 1, 2025 principal installment was not paid, there is a payment Event of Default under Terracotta Section 8.01(a) (no grace period for principal), which is an immediate cross-default under Credit Agreement Section 8.01(f) and makes the no-Default certification false. Any unrecorded amendment (rate or amortization) is a Material Agreement change we have not reviewed. The no-conflicts opinion for the Parent Guarantor must also cover Terracotta.",
 "Obtain the complete executed Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement with all amendments, the payment history, and a Terracotta payoff/status letter confirming principal outstanding and no default. Conform Schedules 5.04 and 7.01. Confirm the character of the $3.5 million in Restricted Payments. Re-certify the excerpts; the current certification contains obvious errors.")
issue("A-3","Korvin License Agreement — anti-pledge clause; consent not obtained","G",
 "Korvin Section 14.2(a) bars any pledge, security interest or encumbrance of the agreement or the License Rights, Licensed Patents or Licensed Technology without Korvin’s consent, which Korvin may withhold in its sole discretion. Section 14.2(b) makes a violating Transfer void *ab initio*. Section 14.3 provides injunctive relief and termination on 30 days’ notice if uncured. Security Agreement Section 2.01(g) expressly grants a lien on “all rights of the Borrower under” the Korvin license. The General Intangibles definition, by contrast, covers Korvin rights only “to the extent assignable or encumberable”, an internal inconsistency. Schedule 5.04 says no consent has been obtained. Credit Agreement Section 5.12 calls the license “material to the conduct of the Borrower’s business”. Security Agreement Section 3.07(d) represents that the IP grant breaches no license and needs no third-party consent; that is false. The Officer’s Certificate cites an Amendment No. 1 (March 15, 2022) that we have not seen. Korvin is mislabeled a “Copyright License” in the Security Agreement. The license term is inconsistent across documents: Korvin “Term” runs to expiry of the last Licensed Patent; Schedule 5.15 says 15 years plus two five-year renewals; Security Agreement Schedule IV says an initial term expiring August 31, 2030. The licensed patents are also described inconsistently (Schedule 5.15 lists U.S. Patent Nos. 9,876,543, 10,234,567 and 10,345,678; Schedule IV refers to a “Korvin European Patent-family”).",
 "This is an actual conflict, carried as Annex F, item 2. Under NY UCC Section 9-408(a) and (c), the anti-assignment clause is ineffective to prevent attachment and perfection of a security interest in the licensee’s general intangible, and to trigger default or termination on account of the grant. Under Section 9-408(d), however, the Agent cannot enforce, use or assign the license against Korvin, so the collateral value is minimal. Whether federal patent law displaces Section 9-408 for an exclusive patent license is unsettled; the draft takes it as qualification (k). The litigation and termination risk is an MAE consideration.",
 "Obtain Korvin’s written consent to the grant, ideally with an estoppel and licensor acknowledgment. If that is not obtainable before closing, amend the Security Agreement to make the Korvin license an Excluded Asset except to the extent Section 9-408 renders the restriction ineffective, and correct Security Agreement Sections 2.01(g) and 3.07(d), Credit Agreement Section 5.03, and the “Copyright License” definition. Obtain the full agreement and Amendment No. 1. Conform the term and patent descriptions.")
issue("A-4","Officer’s Certificate: pro forma covenant failure on a $175 million initial borrowing; wrong sections; historical test","G",
 "Officer’s Certificate Section 4 refers to “the initial borrowing under the Credit Facility in the aggregate principal amount of $175,000,000”. Section 5 and Schedule B test “Section 7.11”, which does not exist; the financial covenants are in Section 7.09. They test only historically as of March 31, 2025, using the Ironbridge balance of $118,750,000, whereas Sections 4.01(e)(iii) and 4.01(l) require pro forma compliance after the initial Borrowing. The FCCR deducts total capex ($8.5 million) rather than Unfinanced Capital Expenditures. No Borrowing Base Certificate has been furnished, and a full $175 million draw requires the Borrowing Base to be at least $175 million.",
 "Using the certificate’s own figures (EBITDA $50.0 million; Subordinated Notes $18.75 million; capital leases and other $5.0 million): a $175 million draw gives Consolidated Funded Indebtedness of $198.75 million and a Total Leverage Ratio of **3.98x**, above the 3.50x maximum. That is an immediate Event of Default under Section 8.01(d) (no cure period), and Section 4.02(c) blocks funding. The largest initial revolving draw consistent with 3.50x is about $151.25 million. A draw equal to the Ironbridge payoff ($118.75 million) produces 2.85x. We do not opine on financial calculations (qualification (n)), but we cannot rely on assumption (7) for a certificate we know to be inaccurate.",
 "Confirm the actual initial Borrowing amount and the Borrowing Base. Re-issue the Officer’s Certificate and deliver the Compliance Certificate (Exhibit B) with a correct Section 7.09 pro forma calculation (including pro forma interest on the new facility and Unfinanced Capex). Delete or correct the $175,000,000 initial-borrowing recital.")

head(d, "B. Authorization, Execution and Incumbency", 2)
issue("B-1","Borrower board authorization — $150 million authorized; board roster conflict; notice; misdescribed subsidiaries","G",
 "The May 28, 2025 minutes, Resolution 1 and Secretary’s Certificate paragraph 6 authorize a facility “up to $150,000,000”, while the Credit Agreement provides $175,000,000. The resolution approves the Credit Agreement “substantially in the form presented” with officer-approved changes; a 16.7% increase in principal is not a conforming change. The minutes record five directors present (Halstead, Nguyen, Sandra L. Whitmore, James E. Carruthers, Robert A. Feinberg) as “the entire membership of the Board”. The Organizational Documents Package, certified by the Secretary on June 12, 2025, lists the directors as Halstead, Nguyen, David T. Okonkwo, Patricia L. Cavanaugh and Robert M. Jennings. Okonkwo appears in the minutes only as a non-director. Bylaws Section 3.2 sets the quorum at a majority of five (three). If the certified roster is correct, only two directors attended and no quorum existed. The minutes cite notice under “Section 3.06” of the Bylaws (48 hours); the Bylaws’ special-meeting notice provision is Section 3.5 (24 hours). The minutes recite both proper notice and waivers from directors “who had not received timely formal notice”. The resolutions describe PFT as a Delaware corporation and PAC as an Ohio corporation (it is the reverse).",
 "Opinion 3(a) (due authorization) cannot be given, and opinion 4 depends on it. Credit Agreement Section 4.01(b)(iii) requires resolutions authorizing the Loan Documents. The Secretary’s Certificate is internally inconsistent with the closing.",
 "Determine the true board composition from stockholder election records or the Parent Guarantor’s stockholder consents. Before signing, have the Borrower’s directors of record adopt a unanimous written consent under DGCL Section 141(f) and Bylaws Section 3.4. The consent should authorize the $175,000,000 facility and each Loan Document by name (Credit Agreement, Security Agreement, Pledge Agreement, Guaranty, Control Agreements), correct the subsidiaries’ jurisdictions, and ratify prior acts. If any act has already occurred, consider DGCL Section 204 ratification. Obtain the notice waivers. Re-issue the Secretary’s Certificate.")
issue("B-2","Parent Guarantor written consent not signed by the directors of record","G",
 "The Tab A consent (May 30, 2025) recites a two-member board (Halstead and Robert J. Castellano) and is signed by those two. The Organizational Documents Package (Part V) says the Parent Guarantor’s bylaws fix a three-member board of Halstead, Nguyen and Patricia L. Cavanaugh, and incorrectly states that the consent was adopted by “all three directors”. DGCL Section 141(f) requires the written consent of all directors in office.",
 "The consent is ineffective unless Castellano is a duly elected director and the board in fact has two members, which contradicts the certified bylaws summary. Opinions 3(b) and 4 cannot be given for the Parent Guarantor (its guaranty, its grant under the Security Agreement, and the pledge of 4,500,000 Borrower shares).",
 "Obtain the complete Parent Guarantor bylaws and director election records. Adopt a new unanimous written consent signed by every director of record that authorizes the Credit Agreement (Article X), Security Agreement, Pledge Agreement and any Guaranty Agreement. Correct the Organizational Documents Package certification.")
issue("B-3","PFT written consent — signed by one purported director; directors do not match the Articles","G",
 "The Tab B consent lists directors Sandra M. Kowalski, James D. Hartwell and Patricia L. Moreno, and only Kowalski signed. PFT’s Articles (Article Fifth) and Code of Regulations (Section 2.1) fix a board of three: Halstead, Nguyen and Okonkwo, “the current directors”. ORC Section 1701.54 and Code Section 2.3 require a writing signed by **all** directors; Section 2.3 says a consent signed by fewer than all directors “shall be of no force or effect”. The consent also states PFT’s principal office as Suite 340, whereas the Articles state Suite 300 and Security Agreement Schedule III states Youngstown, Ohio.",
 "There is no valid PFT authorization, so opinions 3(c) and 4 fail for PFT.",
 "Adopt a new written consent signed by all three directors of record, or evidence a valid change of directors by shareholder action. The consent should approve the Credit Agreement (Article X), the Security Agreement and any Guaranty Agreement by name.")
issue("B-4","PCSS Sole Member consent signed by a person without authority; LLC agreement versions conflict; pledge consent missing","G",
 "The Tab C consent is executed for the Sole Member (the Borrower) by David T. Okonkwo, General Counsel. Under both versions of the PCSS LLC Agreement furnished to us, only the CEO or CFO of the Sole Member is an “Authorized Officer”: Section 2.4 in the Organizational Documents Package version, and Sections 3.2 and 12.4 in the Exhibit 1 “Amended and Restated” version. Section 2.4 expressly excludes the General Counsel. Section 2.3(c)–(d) requires Sole Member consent for any guaranty over $500,000 and **any** grant of a security interest, and makes action without such consent “void and of no force or effect”. Borrower Bylaws Section 4.4 also denies the General Counsel signatory authority over financing documents absent express board authorization. The two LLC agreement versions differ in title, section numbering and consent thresholds: Section 2.3 versus Section 8.3(c), which uses $500,000 individually and $1,000,000 in the aggregate. Section 4.1 bars any pledge of the membership interests without a Member consent executed by an Authorized Officer. No such consent has been delivered for the pledge in Security Agreement Section 2.02(a)(ii).",
 "PCSS’s guaranty and grant are void under its own LLC agreement until a proper consent is delivered, so opinions 3(d), 4 and 7 fail as to PCSS. The pledge of the PCSS interests is also restricted: DLLCA Section 18-1101(g) makes UCC Sections 9-406 and 9-408 inapplicable to LLC interests, so the restriction is enforceable.",
 "Have Halstead or Nguyen re-execute the Sole Member consent, covering the guaranty, Security Agreement grant and Credit Agreement joinder, plus a separate Section 4.1 consent to the pledge of 100% of the PCSS interests. Obtain a certified complete copy of the operative LLC agreement and all amendments. Consider an Article 8 opt-in amendment and certificated interest if the Lenders want control-based priority (Security Agreement Section 4.02(e) contemplates an amendment).")
issue("B-5","PAC written consent — signed by a non-director; a director of record did not sign","G",
 "The Tab D consent recites directors Nguyen and Karen A. Westbrook and is signed by them. PAC’s Certificate of Incorporation (Article V) lists the directors as Halstead and Nguyen and states that a unanimous written consent “requires the consent of both directors.” Halstead did not sign.",
 "The consent fails DGCL Section 141(f), so opinions 3(e) and 4 fail for PAC.",
 "Adopt a new unanimous written consent signed by Halstead and Nguyen, or evidence a valid election of Westbrook, approving the Credit Agreement (Article X), the Security Agreement and any Guaranty Agreement.")
issue("B-6","Signatories and incumbency — guarantor signers are not officers of record; inconsistent across documents; no incumbency certificates","G",
 "PFT signed the Credit Agreement through James A. Whitmore (Vice President) and the Security Agreement through Richard S. Calloway (President). PAC signed through Sandra L. Fujikawa (Vice President) and Jennifer A. Marcos (President), respectively. The governing documents of both PFT and PAC list only Halstead (President) and Nguyen (Secretary/Treasurer) as officers. Each guarantor consent authorizes “any officer”, but no evidence of these individuals’ appointment and no incumbency certificate has been furnished for the Parent Guarantor, PFT, PCSS or PAC (Credit Agreement Section 4.01(b)(iv)). The Agent’s signatory appears as “Christopher D. Cromdale Consulting” in the Credit Agreement and “Christopher D. Engelman” in the Security Agreement. “Cromdale Consulting” is also the name of the securities intermediary in Schedule V, which suggests a document-assembly error.",
 "The execution and delivery limb of opinion 3 cannot be given. The genuineness assumption (assumption 1) excludes Opinion Party officers, so we must verify the signers’ incumbency.",
 "Either have Halstead or Nguyen execute for PFT and PAC, or deliver board resolutions appointing the named officers together with incumbency and specimen-signature certificates for every Opinion Party. Flag the Agent signature-block errors to Drummond.")
issue("B-7","Organizational documents — excerpts only; certification defects","H",
 "The Organizational Documents Package contains excerpts only, certified by the General Counsel. It describes the facility’s agent as “National Union Bank, N.A., as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent”, refers to the opinion as delivered under Section 4.01(e) (it is 4.01(d)), and refers to an Officer’s Certificate dated June 10, 2025 that is not in the file. Credit Agreement Section 4.01(b)(i) requires charters certified by the Secretary of State, and Drummond’s letter requires our review of the organizational documents themselves.",
 "Opinions 1, 2, 3 and 5(i) rest on complete governing documents. An excerpt-based review is insufficient, particularly given the director and officer discrepancies above.",
 "Obtain Secretary of State-certified charters (bring-down dated within 10 Business Days), complete bylaws, Code of Regulations and LLC agreement, and a corrected Secretary’s Certificate for each Opinion Party.")

issue("C-1","PFT Ohio good standing certificate is stale","H",
 "The PFT certificate is dated April 12, 2025 (a Saturday), about 64 days before closing. Credit Agreement Section 4.01(c) and the June 9 letter require certificates dated within 10 Business Days of closing. Counting back from June 15, 2025 (a Sunday), the earliest acceptable date is June 2, 2025.",
 "Opinion 1(c) is bracketed pending the bring-down.",
 "Order an Ohio Certificate of Good Standing for PFT today.")
issue("C-2","Borrower foreign-qualification certificates missing (MI, IN, TX, CA)","H",
 "Schedule 5.13(C) and Section 5.01(c) list Ohio, Michigan, Indiana, Texas and California. Only Ohio (June 3, 2025) was obtained. Drummond’s letter specifically calls out all five states. The Organizational Documents Package relies on a General Counsel representation for the other four states.",
 "The foreign good standing opinion is limited to Ohio unless the certificates arrive. That fails a specific Lender requirement and Section 4.01(c).",
 "Order certificates from Michigan LARA, the Indiana Secretary of State, the Texas Secretary of State or Comptroller (account status), and the California Secretary of State. If timing fails, Drummond must agree in writing to a post-closing delivery.")
issue("C-3","Subsidiary Guarantor foreign qualification — conflicting record; nothing obtained","H",
 "Schedule 5.13(D) states that PFT is qualified in MI and IN, PCSS in OH and TX, and PAC in OH, TX and CA. The Organizational Documents Package (Part VI) states that none of them is qualified outside its home state. Schedule 5.17 shows leased operating facilities for PFT in Fort Wayne, IN, PCSS in Houston, TX, and PAC in El Segundo, CA, and all three show Akron, Ohio offices. The Good Standing Summary requested foreign certificates for the Borrower only, although Section 4.01(c) covers each Loan Party. The Parent Guarantor’s principal office is in Akron, Ohio, but it is reportedly not qualified in Ohio.",
 "Either Schedule 5.13 and the Section 5.01(c) representation are wrong, or the subsidiaries (and possibly the Parent Guarantor) are doing business unqualified in states where they operate. The draft declines the “where required” formulation (a factual matter under TriBar practice) and brackets the subsidiary foreign opinions.",
 "Confirm actual qualifications with the client and through state searches. Qualify where needed (Indiana, Texas, California and Ohio appear to be implicated), obtain certificates, and correct Schedule 5.13.")
issue("C-4","Inconsistent certificate dates and entity file numbers","M",
 "The Good Standing Summary gives PCSS June 6 and PAC June 7; the Organizational Documents Package gives PCSS June 7 and PAC June 6. Delaware and Ohio file numbers differ across the record (see the table below). The Organizational Documents Package also gives an Ohio foreign registration number of 2090215 for the Borrower, while the Search Report gives F-2148703.",

 "Check every certificate and search certificate against the Secretary of State records, and correct Security Agreement Schedule III.")

head(d, "D. Collateral, Perfection and Priority", 2)
issue("D-1","Ironbridge all-assets UCC-1 not terminated; prior facility facts inconsistent","G",
 "Delaware File No. 2019-4572810 (filed August 9, 2019; continued July 22, 2024 to August 9, 2029) covers all of the Borrower’s assets. No UCC-3 termination was of record on June 8, 2025. The Credit Agreement dates the Prior Credit Facility March 15, 2019. Terracotta Schedule 5.11 (April 2021) shows Ironbridge as a $100 million facility maturing August 9, 2024. The Officer’s Certificate shows $118.75 million outstanding in 2025.",
 "Ironbridge’s earlier filing would prime the Agent under UCC Section 9-322(a)(1) while it secures obligations. Section 4.01(g) is unsatisfied, and opinion 7(g) is bracketed.",
 "Obtain the Ironbridge payoff letter (amount, per diem, automatic lien release, authorization for the Borrower or Agent to file the UCC-3, and return of possessory collateral). File the UCC-3 at funding and obtain filed-stamped evidence. Reconcile the facility size and maturity (extension or upsizing amendments).")
issue("D-2","Unreleased $347,218.64 Ohio state tax lien against the Borrower","G",
 "Ohio Secretary of State notice OH-2024-TL-0048271 (March 3, 2024) covers all property for taxes, penalties and interest under ORC Chapters 5739 and 5747. It does not appear on Schedule 7.02. It contradicts Credit Agreement Section 5.08 (no tax liens filed) and is likely not a Permitted Lien: clause (i) covers only taxes not yet delinquent or contested in good faith with reserves. The Search Report itself has reliability problems. It names the claimant as a “Great Lakes Tax Authority, Ohio Department of Revenue” (Ohio’s agency is the Department of Taxation). It describes Chapter 5739 as the commercial activity tax (Chapter 5739 is sales and use tax; the CAT is Chapter 5751). And Ohio tax liens are typically recorded as judgment liens with the county clerk of courts, which were not searched. The Search Report also cites the wrong Credit Agreement sections (5.08/5.09 rather than 5.07/5.08).",
 "A statutory tax lien may prime the Agent regardless of filing priority, so we give no priority opinion over it (Annex G, Part 2). The Officer’s Certificate representations are inaccurate.",
 "Obtain a certified copy of the lien notice and confirm the claimant and the underlying assessment. Pay the lien and file a release before closing (fund from proceeds with a release in escrow if necessary). If it is contested, add it to Schedule 7.02 with reserves and disclose it. Correct Section 5.08 and the Officer’s Certificate. Run Summit County (and other county) judgment and tax-lien searches.")
issue("D-3","Aldersgate filing — true lease or security interest?","M",
 "The Search Report treats Aldersgate as a precautionary true-lease filing. Credit Agreement Schedule 7.01 lists it as “Capital Lease Obligations … Secured by leased equipment” (about $4.8 million). **WHITFIELD & CRANE LLP**

**MEMORANDUM**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **To:**                             **Victoria S. Engstrom, Partner**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **cc:**                             Marcus J. Wellbourne, Associate; W&C Opinion Committee

  **From:**                           Opinion drafting team

  **Date:**                           June 12, 2025

  **Re:**                             Pinnacle Manufacturing Group, Inc. --- \$175,000,000 Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility (Ridgeline National Bank, as Administrative Agent) --- Closing Opinion: Deficiencies in Closing Documents and Required Cures
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Part I --- Bottom Line

The accompanying advance draft of our closing opinion (closing-legal-opinion.docx) follows the June 9, 2025 requirements letter from Raymond K. Drummond (Drummond & Associates LLP). It addresses each of the five Opinion Parties separately on each opinion topic. **On the current record we cannot deliver the opinion in the form the Lender Parties requested, and several defects are also failures of Credit Agreement closing conditions.** The draft therefore brackets every opinion that depends on a cure, carries the actual conflicts as specific exceptions (no materiality qualifier, as Drummond asked), and flags each non-standard assumption and qualification for Lender counsel. Drummond's letter asks us to advise "as soon as possible" if we foresee any inability to deliver a requested opinion; we recommend sending the draft today with the cover note in Part VI.

The gating items, in order of severity:

- **Terracotta covenant breach (Issue A-1).** The \$175,000,000 of commitments breaches the \$125,000,000 Senior Secured Indebtedness cap (undrawn commitments included) in Section 7.01(b) of the Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement. That breach ripens into a Terracotta Event of Default and then a cross-default under Credit Agreement Section 8.01(f). A Terracotta amendment or consent is required, or the commitments must be cut to about \$120.1 million.

- **Korvin consent (Issue A-3).** The Security Agreement grants a lien on the Borrower's rights under the Korvin License Agreement without the consent Section 14.2 requires. Without consent the grant is void as between the parties, and Korvin may terminate a license the Credit Agreement itself calls material.

- **Authorizations (Part B).** None of the five entity authorizations supports a due-authorization opinion. The Borrower authorized only \$150 million, and its board roster conflicts with the certified records. The Parent Guarantor, PFT and PAC consents were signed by persons who are not (or not all) the directors of record. The PCSS consent was signed by the General Counsel, who the LLC agreement says cannot act for the member. The guarantor signatories do not appear as officers in the governing documents.

- **Priority (Issues D-1 and D-2).** The Ironbridge all-assets UCC-1 has not been terminated (it is continued to 2029). There is also an unreleased \$347,218.64 Ohio state tax lien against the Borrower that is not on Schedule 7.02.

- **Officer's Certificate and pro forma covenants (Issue A-4).** The certificate recites an initial borrowing of \$175,000,000. On its own numbers, that produces pro forma Total Leverage of about 3.98x against a 3.50x maximum (an immediate Event of Default with no cure period), and the certificate tests the wrong section on a historical rather than pro forma basis.

- **Good standing (Part C).** The PFT Ohio certificate is stale (April 12, 2025). The Borrower's Michigan, Indiana, Texas and California certificates are missing. The record conflicts on whether the Subsidiary Guarantors are qualified anywhere outside their home states.

# Part II --- Documents Reviewed

Requirements letter (Drummond, June 9, 2025); Credit Agreement dated as of June 15, 2025 (with Schedules 2.01, 5.04, 5.06, 5.13, 5.15, 5.17, 7.01, 7.02 and Exhibit C); Security Agreement dated as of June 15, 2025 (with Schedules I--V); minutes of the Borrower's May 28, 2025 special board meeting and Secretary's Certificate; Subsidiary and Guarantor Authorizations Package (Tabs A--D and Exhibit 1); Organizational Documents Package (excerpts, certified by D. Okonkwo June 12, 2025); Good Standing Certificates Summary (June 15, 2025); Officer's Certificate (June 15, 2025) with Exhibit A and Schedules A and B; UCC Search Results Report (compiled June 12, 2025; searches through June 8, 2025); Subordinated Note Purchase Agreement excerpts; Korvin Technology License Agreement excerpts.

I've produced both deliverables. Both pass the docx skill's validate.py and parse back cleanly with parse-doc. The main finding is that the opinion can't be delivered in the form the lenders asked for on the current record. The opinion is therefore an advance draft for lender counsel: every opinion that depends on a fix is bracketed, and each problem is explained in a "Note to Draft."

**closing-legal-opinion.docx** is on Whitfield & Crane's Cleveland letterhead and addressed to Ridgeline (as Administrative Agent) and each Lender. It follows the June 9 requirements letter from Drummond (lender counsel):
- It covers the named transaction documents and addresses each of the five companies separately on each topic: existence and good standing, power, authorization/execution/delivery, enforceability, no conflicts, no governmental approvals, security interests, and litigation.
- Assumptions are the seven the lenders accepted. Three extra ones (including treating New York law as identical to Ohio law, since every document picks New York law) are bracketed and flagged for Drummond's agreement.
- All qualifications are listed in full, with no "customary exceptions" shorthand. Extra ones are bracketed and flagged.
- Security interests are addressed by collateral type:
  - Creation is under New York UCC Article 9.
  - Perfection by filing is in Delaware and Ohio.
  - Deposit accounts are covered by control: automatic for accounts at Ridgeline itself, and by control agreement for the others.
  - Securities accounts are covered by control agreement.
  - Pledged stock is covered by control and by filing. The PCSS membership interests are general intangibles perfected by filing.
  - Registered copyrights are excluded.
- On priority, it declines a general "first-priority" opinion. It gives priority opinions based on the search report and on control of the pledged stock, and addresses each prior filing the search found.
- Annexes cover the lender list, a party-by-document matrix, the financing statements, the accounts, the good standing certificates and pledged equity, two specific no-conflicts exceptions, the priority filings, and the pending litigation.

**opinion-issues-memo.docx** is an internal memo to Victoria Engstrom (the partner) with a bottom line, 28 issues rated by severity (each with sources, effect on the opinion and fix), a summary matrix, a closing deliverables checklist and a draft cover note to Drummond. The issues that block delivery:
- **Terracotta notes cap:** the $175M commitments breach the subordinated note agreement's $125M cap on senior secured debt, which counts undrawn commitments (§7.01(b)). That leads to a Terracotta default and then a cross-default under Credit Agreement §8.01(f). Without an amendment, the commitments would have to drop to about $120.1M.
- **Terracotta payments:** the note agreement's annual amortization would leave $15.625M outstanding, not the $18.75M reported. Either there is an unseen amendment or the April 1, 2025 principal payment may have been missed.
- **Korvin license:** the Security Agreement takes a lien on the Korvin license without the consent §14.2 requires, and the purported grant is void under the license's own terms. UCC §9-408 keeps the lien attached and blocks termination for the grant, but the Agent couldn't enforce or use the license against Korvin.
- **Officer's Certificate:** it recites a $175M initial borrowing. On its own figures that gives total leverage of about 3.98x against a 3.50x maximum, an immediate default. It also tests the wrong section (7.11 instead of 7.09) and on a historical rather than pro forma basis.
- **Authorizations, all five companies:**
  - The Borrower's board approved only $150M, and the directors at the meeting don't match the certified board list, so there may have been no quorum.
  - The consents for Pinnacle Holdings (the parent) and Pinnacle Aerospace weren't signed by the directors of record.
  - Pinnacle Fastener's was signed by one of three listed directors, who aren't the directors of record either.
  - The PCSS consent was signed by the General Counsel, whom the LLC agreement bars from acting for the member.
  - The people signing for Pinnacle Fastener and Pinnacle Aerospace aren't officers of record, and there are no incumbency certificates.
- **Prior liens:** the old lender's (Ironbridge) all-assets UCC-1 is still on file, continued to 2029, and there is an unscheduled $347,218.64 Ohio tax lien against the Borrower.
- **Good standing:** the Pinnacle Fastener certificate is stale (April 12, 2025). The Borrower's Michigan, Indiana, Texas and California certificates are missing, and the record conflicts on whether the subsidiaries are qualified outside their home states.

Other points in the memo:
- The closing date, June 15, 2025, is a Sunday, which isn't a Business Day under the Credit Agreement.
- Share counts in the pledge schedule are wrong for Pinnacle Fastener and Pinnacle Aerospace.
- Entity file numbers conflict across three documents.
- The IP schedules in the Credit Agreement and Security Agreement don't match.
- The UCC searches have gaps.
- The control agreements, Pledge Agreement and any separate Guaranty Agreement were never provided, so the draft can't opine on them yet.
